article_content: A jury at London’s Old Bailey acquitted 25-year-old Annie Merrilees of murder after deliberating for less than three hours. She admitted to stabbing her boyfriend, Dean Williamson, 31, but insisted it was in self-defense after enduring three years of violent abuse. Merrilees, a former Harrods employee and mother of two, told the court that Williamson — a nightclub bouncer with a history of cocaine use and aggression — had repeatedly beaten her, even while she was nearly eight months pregnant. On the night of the incident, she said he forced his way into their shared home in Chadwell Heath, Essex, grabbed her by the throat, and threatened her violently. Fearing for her life, she grabbed a nearby knife and stabbed him in the chest. She did not intend to kill him, she testified, adding, 'I loved him. I just wanted him to leave.' Though prosecutors acknowledged Williamson’s violent past and substance abuse, they argued that Merrilees also engaged in heated arguments and used drugs, suggesting the relationship was mutually volatile. Neighbors reportedly described her as sometimes more confrontational than Williamson. However, no witness saw the stabbing itself. A friend, Katie O’Brien, recalled seeing Williamson clutch his chest after emerging from the bedroom, whispering, 'Stabbed, Kate,' before collapsing. He died the next day after emergency heart surgery. Merrilees initially told police Williamson had injured himself with the knife, but later retracted that claim through her lawyer, confirming she acted in fear for her safety. The judge, Christopher Moss QC, told her, 'You are free to go,' as she quietly mouthed 'thank you' to the jury. Her family wept with relief. The court heard Williamson had prior convictions, including an unproven link to an armed robbery. Ultimately, the jury believed her account of sustained abuse and imminent threat — and found her not guilty of both murder and manslaughter.

article_content: By Daniel Martin. Secretary of State for Communities and Local Government Eric Pickles has confirmed that two 'garden cities' could be built in the southeast to help tackle Britain's housing crisis. Pickles insisted these developments would not be imposed on communities without their consent, noting that several local councils have already expressed interest. He clarified that his department did not produce a recent draft report suggesting new settlements in Yalding, Kent, and Gerrards Cross, Buckinghamshire. Speaking on Sky News’s Murnaghan programme, Pickles emphasized that no final decisions have been made on locations. 'Let me be absolutely clear: I have not seen this report, formally or informally—it does not come from my department,' he said. 'While we are the experts in planning and housing and would naturally be involved, I don’t rule out that an ambitious civil servant from another department drafted it.' 'Both parties stood on a manifesto committing not to force eco-towns or garden cities on the public,' he added. Pickles noted that the coalition government is releasing land through its Local Infrastructure Plan, with plots for 100,000 homes expected to be available before the next election. 'It is vital to establish settlements where infrastructure—roads, utilities, schools—is already in place or planned,' he said. 'We could build one or two garden cities, but only where communities want them and local authorities are on board.' He criticized past Labour policies, stating: 'Labour promised five garden cities and delivered none. Then they promised ten. All they achieved was public resentment—not a single home.' In a recent Daily Telegraph article, Deputy Prime Minister Nick Clegg wrote: 'We cannot repeat the mistakes of past governments by sitting idle while a generation is priced out of the housing market. It is our duty to change the story.' 'We must end decades of indecision and stagnant political will,' Clegg continued. 'That’s why I strongly support garden cities—with clear local support and private sector engagement. In 2011, our housing strategy pledged to publish a prospectus for new garden cities—and that is precisely what we will do.'

article_content: A Brown University student tested positive for GHB—a colorless, odorless sedative commonly used in drug-facilitated sexual assaults—after consuming punch at a fraternity party on October 17. The same party was attended by another female student who alleges she was sexually assaulted after drinking the same punch; her toxicology results are still pending. Campus officials at Brown, located in Providence, Rhode Island, issued a warning to students via email, highlighting the dangers of GHB, which can cause rapid intoxication and memory loss far beyond what the amount of alcohol consumed would suggest. Margaret Klawunn, cited in the Providence Journal report, described both students experiencing extreme and unexplained sedation. In response to the incident, the Phi Kappa Psi fraternity has been suspended—not for the alleged assault or drugging, but for hosting an alcohol-serving event without university approval. Fraternity members have strongly denied any involvement in the incidents, stating in a letter to the college newspaper that no member has been accused or criminally charged with sexual assault or drugging. They emphasized their confidence that no member engaged in such criminal behavior. Brown University has affirmed that if the allegations are true, they violate university conduct policies, Rhode Island state law, and community values. Students with relevant information are encouraged to contact university police.

Samme fest blev besøgt af en anden kvindelig studerende, der påstår, at hun blev voldtaget efter at have drukket samme punch; hendes toksikologiske resultater er stadig ude. article_content: Over the past two years, millions of Americans have seen their federal student debt erased thanks to new initiatives from the Biden administration. Now, even more relief is on the horizon—for those who left school decades ago, those in public service, and those misled by their colleges. One major change is the IDR Account Adjustment: the Department of Education is now counting time spent in any repayment plan—including deferments and forbearances—as credit toward the 20- or 25-year forgiveness timeline, even if borrowers never enrolled in an income-driven plan. More than 800,000 people have already benefited, especially those who graduated before 2003 (undergraduates) or 1998 (graduate students). But not all periods count: in-school deferments, defaults, and short-term forbearances are excluded. There’s also a valuable opportunity: consolidating loans via the Direct Loan program before December 31, 2023 lets borrowers apply credit from their oldest loan to their entire consolidated balance. Separately, a new program under the Higher Education Act is being crafted to help borrowers whose loans entered repayment 25 years ago. While details are still being finalized through public hearings, the goal is clear: forgive those who’ve paid for decades without relief. Public servants who never applied for PSLF might also qualify if they worked for 10 years since 2007, even if they didn’t realize it. And starting July 1, 2024, the SAVE plan will cut forgiveness time for low-balance borrowers: anyone who borrowed $12,000 or less will see their remaining balance wiped clean after just 10 years of payments, with the cap increasing by one year for every extra $1,000 borrowed.

Et af de vigtigste ændringer er IDR-kontojusteringen: Uddannelsesdepartementet tæller nu tid, der er brugt i ethvert tilbagebetalingsprogram—inklusiv udsættelse og opskud—as kredit mod den 20- eller 25-årige sletningsfrist, selvom låntagerne aldrig har deltaget i et indkomstbaseret betalingsplan. article_content: Liverpool secured a thrilling 3-2 victory over Tottenham Hotspur at Anfield, extending their unbeaten Premier League run to nine matches and reigniting their top-four ambitions. With the win, they now sit just three points behind fourth-placed Arsenal. The decisive moment came in the 83rd minute when Mario Balotelli, starting in place of the injured Daniel Sturridge, tapped in a clinical finish to seal the win—his first league goal since his £16 million move from AC Milan last summer. Tottenham twice clawed back from behind: Harry Kane equalized after Lazar Markovic’s opener, and Mousa Dembele leveled again after Steven Gerrard restored Liverpool’s lead from the penalty spot. Despite the drama, Liverpool displayed resilience and composure. Captain Steven Gerrard, who celebrated his penalty with characteristic passion, was substituted in the final stages due to a hamstring concern, prompting cautious concern from the coaching staff. Assistant coach Colin Pascoe, speaking in manager Brendan Rodgers’ absence, praised Balotelli’s work rate and impact: 'He worked hard, got the goal, and got the three points. I hope this is a springboard.' Tottenham manager Mauricio Pochettino felt a draw was a fair outcome, citing his side’s strong performance and early defensive lapses. 'We deserved more,' he said, though acknowledged the intensity of the contest. Youngster Jordon Ibe impressed with a key assist, while Daniel Sturridge remained a constant threat. For Liverpool, the win was a statement of intent; for Spurs, a bitter pill after a spirited display.

Med sejren ligger de kun tre point bag fjerdepladsen, som er besat af Arsenal. Det afgørende øjeblik kom i den 83. minut, da Mario Balotelli, der startede i stedet for den skadede Daniel Sturridge, ramte en præcis afslutning for at sikre sejren – hans første liga-mål siden sin £16-millioners-overgang fra AC Milan for et år siden. Tottenham kom to gange tilbage fra bagud: Harry Kane udligede efter Lazar Markovics åbner, og Mousa Dembele ligejede igen efter Steven Gerrard havde genoprettet Liverpools fordel fra straffespark. Trods dramatikken viste Liverpool mod og ro. Kapten Steven Gerrard, der fejrede sit straffespark med karakteristisk entusiasme, blev skiftet ud i de sidste minutter på grund af en hamstringbekymring, hvilket skabte forsigtig bekymring blandt trænerstaben. Assisterende træner Colin Pascoe, der talte i manager Brendan Rodgers’ fravær, lovpriste Balotellis arbejdsevne og indflydelse: 'Han arbejdede hårdt, scorede målet og fik de tre point. Jeg håber, dette kan være en springbræt.' Tottenham-manager Mauricio Pochettino mente, at et uafgjort resultat var rimeligt, og pegede på holdets stærke præstation og tidlige defensive fejl. 'Vi fortjente mere,' sagde han, men anerkendte kampens intensitet. Ungdommen Jordon Ibe imponerede med en afgørende assist, mens Daniel Sturridge forblev en konstant trussel. For Liverpool var sejren et udsagn om intentioner; for Spurs en bitter pille efter en levende præstation.

article_content: New York (CNN) — Sulaiman Abu Ghaith, a former Al Qaeda propagandist and son-in-law of Osama bin Laden, spent a long flight last week bound for New York — and ultimately, a jail cell just blocks from Ground Zero. During the journey, he spoke at length with U.S. investigators, offering statements that could play a pivotal role in his upcoming trial. His capture marked the end of a winding path that began weeks earlier in Iran. According to Turkish media, Abu Ghaith left Iran under unclear circumstances and crossed into Turkey using a forged Saudi passport. The CIA traced him to a hotel room in Turkey, where he was detained by local authorities in early February. Yet, Turkish officials delayed handing him over to the U.S. for nearly a month. Instead, they deported him to Kuwait — his birthplace — hoping to distance themselves from the controversy. But U.S. law enforcement intercepted him during a layover in Jordan. Members of the High Value Interrogation Group (HIG), which includes CIA operatives, were involved in the operation. Abu Ghaith reportedly spoke freely during the flight with U.S. agents, providing details now believed to be documented in a 22-page statement. The Justice Department and FBI have declined to confirm whether Abu Ghaith was read his Miranda rights after arrest — a legal requirement if his statements are to be used in court. Experts like Mitchell Silber, former NYPD intelligence director and now with K2 Intelligence, note that while Abu Ghaith has been out of Al Qaeda’s inner circle since 2002 — living under house arrest in Iran — his insights into Tehran’s relationship with other senior Al Qaeda figures may still hold value. Iran hosts several high-ranking former Al Qaeda members under surveillance, and U.S. officials are keen to understand the nature of this uneasy alliance. Are the predominantly Shiite Iranians cooperating with, controlling, or merely containing these Sunni extremists? Could they be exploiting them? Abu Ghaith may be one of the few who can answer. On Friday, Abu Ghaith appeared in a Manhattan federal courtroom, handcuffed and flanked by U.S. marshals, less than a mile from the site of the 9/11 attacks. His attorney, Philip Weinstein, entered a not guilty plea on his behalf. Abu Ghaith told the judge, through an Arabic interpreter, that he could not afford legal representation. His statements remain sealed, and he remains in custody without bail until his next court date in April. A trial date has not yet been scheduled. If convicted, he faces life imprisonment.

Abu Ghaith skal have talt frit under flyvningen med amerikanske agenters, og hans udsagn antages at være dokumenteret i en 22-siders erklæring. Hans advokat, Philip Weinstein, indgav en ikke-skyldig-erklæring på hans vegne. Abu Ghaith fortalte dommeren gennem en arabisk tolk, at han ikke kunne betale for en advokat. Hans udsagn er stadig hemmelige, og han holdes i fangenskab uden kaution indtil hans næste høring i april. En retssagsdato er endnu ikke fastsat. Hvis han dømmes skyldig, risikerer han livsvarigt fængsel.

article_content: LONDON, England (CNN) — A new robotic exoskeleton could transform the lives of people with paralysis, enabling them to walk again. The device, called ReWalk, is a lightweight system comprising motorized leg supports and advanced motion sensors. Users wear a backpack containing a computerized control unit that detects intent to step and activates movement accordingly. 'Standing changes my entire environment. I no longer have to look up at people — now I’m eye to eye with everyone,' said Radi Kaiof, a former Israeli soldier paralyzed from the waist down for two decades. Although he lacks sensation in his legs, ReWalk allows him to stand and walk with the aid of crutches for balance. With this device, individuals paralyzed from the waist down can walk, bend, sit, and even climb stairs — offering a viable alternative to wheelchairs for those with functional upper bodies. ReWalk was developed by Dr. Amit Goffer, an engineer and founder of Argo Medical Technologies based in Haifa, Israel. Goffer was inspired to create the device more than ten years ago after becoming disabled in an accident. Though not yet available for purchase, ReWalk entered clinical trials in Tel Aviv in late 2007. Additional trials are planned in the United States and Europe. If regulatory approvals are granted, the device could reach the market in 2010. The final price has not been set, but it is expected to align with the average annual cost of wheelchair maintenance and related care. According to Goffer, ReWalk enhances users’ physical health by promoting daily activity and, more importantly, restores dignity — 'the number one issue' for people using wheelchairs. For Kaiof, the device has been life-changing: his daughter had never seen him stand until he wore ReWalk. 'She couldn’t believe how tall I was,' he told CNN.

Brukere bærer en ryggsekk med en datamaskinbasert kontrollenhet som oppdager intensjonen til å ta et skritt og aktiverer bevegelsen. 'Å stå endrer hele mitt miljø. Selv om han ikke har følelse i beina, tillater ReWalk ham å stå og gå med hjelp av staver for balanse. Med denne enheten kan personer paralyserede fra midjen og ned gå, bøye seg, sitte og selv klatre trapper — og tilby en alternativ løsning til rullestol for de med funksjonelle overkropper. ReWalk ble utviklet av Dr. Amit Goffer, en ingeniør og grunnlegger av Argo Medical Technologies i Haifa, Israel. Den endelige prisen er ikke fastsatt, men den forventes å være i samme størrelsesorden som de gjennomsnittlige årlige kostnadene ved rullestolvedlikehold og relatert omsorg. Ifølge Goffer forbedrer ReWalk brukernes fysiske helse ved å fremme daglig aktivitet og, viktigst av alt, gjenoppretter verdighet — 'det viktigste problemet' for mennesker som bruker rullestoler. For Kaiof har enheten forandret livet: hans datter hadde aldri sett ham stå før han brukte ReWalk. 'Hun kunne ikke tro hvor høy jeg var,' sa han til CNN.

article_content: By Daily Mail Reporter. Published: 21:48 EST, 11 August 2013. Updated: 05:43 EST, 12 August 2013. The father of four-year-old Kyrillos Gendy has spoken out in anguish after his son was struck and killed by a car while crossing the street near a bagel shop in Staten Island. Kyrillos was with his mother, Arini Thomas, and his seven-year-old sister, Gabriella, at the time. John Sanjurjo, a 33-year-old former Air Force serviceman, turned himself in to police 16 hours after the incident and pleaded not guilty during his court appearance. He was released on $50,000 bail. 'You got the wrong guy, man,' Sanjurjo said as he entered the courtroom. Reda Gendy, the boy’s father, responded emotionally: 'He could have at least waited until I buried my son.' He told ABC 7, 'I’m going to send him a postcard of my son every single birthday so he can know what he took from me.' Sanjurjo faces charges of leaving the scene of an accident, which carries a potential seven-year prison sentence if convicted. His defense attorney, Anthony Caronna, argued that the prosecution has no direct evidence linking Sanjurjo to the wheel—only that the vehicle was registered to him. 'The complaint is insufficient on its face,' Caronna told SI Live. Arini Thomas sustained a head injury in the crash. Kyrillos suffered severe head trauma and internal bleeding. Despite being revived twice at Staten Island University Hospital, he died during surgery due to critically low blood pressure. Witnesses, including Mahmoud Odeh, owner of the nearby deli, described the scene: 'The mother was scared, holding her son. He was bleeding from the nose and mouth and not moving. She was praying loudly.' Security footage from the bagel shop captured the vehicle entering the parking lot. Authorities are reviewing it as part of the investigation. Family members expressed shock that Sanjurjo was not charged with manslaughter. 'I think it's ridiculous he’s not being charged with manslaughter at the very least,' said cousin Adam Gendy to NBC 4. 'He had his whole life in front of him. I feel like he has been stolen from us.' Reda Gendy, overcome with grief, added: 'Had he run to my son and held him as he took his last breath, that would have meant more to me. I’m going to let him live with the fact that he took life from me.'

article_content: An aid convoy that came under fire in a besieged neighborhood in Homs delivered only a portion of its supplies before withdrawing, the Syrian Red Crescent said Saturday. 'Although our team was shelled and fired upon, we managed to deliver 250 food parcels, 190 hygiene kits, and medicines for chronic diseases,' the organization said in a tweet. One driver sustained a minor injury when explosions and gunfire struck near the convoy. The convoy departed, leaving behind two damaged trucks. Valerie Amos, the UN humanitarian chief, lamented that the 'three-day humanitarian pause agreed upon was broken today, and aid workers were deliberately targeted.' She added, 'Today’s events serve as a stark reminder of the dangers civilians and aid workers face every day across Syria,' praising the 'courage and tenacity' of UN and Red Crescent staff. Video footage posted by activists showed bullet holes in aid vehicles and explosion damage to nearby buildings. The state-run Syrian Arab News Agency (SANA) reported that four Syrian Red Crescent workers were wounded by gunfire from 'terrorist groups' while attempting to deliver aid to Homs’ Old City. Homs Governor Talal al-Barazi claimed that 'armed terrorist groups' violated a truce by firing mortar shells at a police command center in the Old Sa’a area. However, he affirmed the government’s commitment to helping civilians evacuate the Old City. The UN-led operation to evacuate civilians began Friday, with 83 women, children, and elderly residents allowed to leave following a ceasefire agreement between the government and opposition groups — intended also to enable aid delivery on Saturday. An estimated 2,500 civilians remain trapped in Homs, parts of which have been under siege since June 2012. A video posted Saturday on YouTube showed more than a dozen civilians walking between four UN vehicles — two on each side — likely to avoid gunfire. It was unclear whether they reached safety. Violence flared across Syria on Saturday, with at least 83 people killed, including 10 children and six women, according to the Local Coordination Committees of Syria. Five of the deaths occurred in Homs; 41 were in Aleppo. Video from Aleppo, posted by an opposition activist, depicted the aftermath of what was described as a government helicopter barrel-bomb attack: buildings reduced to rubble, dismembered bodies, and burning vehicles. Barrel bombs are crude explosive devices made from drums filled with explosives and shrapnel. U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry condemned the attacks, stating: 'Each and every barrel bomb filled with metal shrapnel and fuel launched against innocent Syrians underscores the barbarity of a regime that has turned its country into a super-magnet for terror.'

'Selvom vores hold blev beskudt og skudt på, lykkedes det os at levere 250 madpakker, 190 hygiejnekits og medicin til kroniske sygdomme,' sagde organisationen i en tweet. En chauffør fik en let skade, da eksplosioner og skyderi ramte nær konvojen. Konvojen forlod området og efterlod to beskadigede lastbiler. Valerie Amos, FN's humanitære chef, udtrykte sin sorg over, at 'den tre-dages humanitære pause, som var blevet aftalt, blev brudt i dag, og hjælpearbejdere blev bevidst målrettet.' Hun tilføjede: 'Dagens begivenheder er en skræmmende påmindelse om de farer, civile og hjælpearbejdere står overfor hver dag i Syrien,' og lovpriste 'mod og vedholdenhed' hos FN- og Røde-Kors-hjælpearbejdere. Video fra scenen, uploadet af aktivister, viste kuglehuller i hjælpeførtøjet og skader fra eksplosioner på nærliggende bygninger. Den statslige syriske nyhedsagentur SANA rapporterede, at fire arbejdere fra Det Syriske Røde Kors blev såret af skyderi fra 'terrorister' mens de forsøgte at levere humanitær hjælp til Homs gamle by. Homs guvernør Talal al-Barazi påstod, at 'våbnede terrorister' brød en våbenstilstand ved at skyde mortergranater mod et politiskommando i Old Sa’a. Men han bekræftede, at regeringen ville holde sit løfte om at hjælpe civile med at forlade Homs gamle by. Den FN-ledede operation til at evakuere civile begyndte fredag, hvor 83 kvinder, børn og ældre blev tilladt at forlade byen efter en våbenstilstands-aftale mellem regeringen og oppositionen — også med henblik på at tillade humanitær hjælp at nå byen lørdag. Op til 2.500 civile antages at være fanget i Homs, hvor dele af byen har været belægren siden juni 2012. En video uploadet lørdag på YouTube viste mere end et dusin civile, der gik mellem fire FN-biler — to på hver side — sandsynligvis for at undgå skyderi. Det var ikke klart, om de nåede til deres destination. Volden flammede op igen i hele Syrien lørdag, med mindst 83 dræbte, herunder 10 børn og seks kvinder, ifølge Local Coordination Committees of Syria. Fem af dødsfaldene skete i Homs; 41 i Aleppo. Video fra Aleppo, uploadet af en oppositionsaktivist, viste følgerne af, hvad der blev beskrevet som et regeringshelikopter-barrel-bomb-angreb: bygninger med ansigtet sprængt af, lig med afskårne lemmer og brandende biler. Barrel-bomber er primitive eksplosive enheder lavet af tønder fyldt med eksplosiver og splinter. USA's udenrigsminister John Kerry fordømte angrebene og sagde: 'Hvert eneste barrel bomb fyldt med metal splinter og brændstof, der bliver affyret mod uskyldige syrere, understreger barbariet hos et regime, der har gjort sit land til en supermagnet for terror.'

article_content: Photographs of David Cameron phoning Barack Obama to congratulate him on winning a second term were intended to highlight the growing friendship between the two leaders. However, closer inspection reveals that the Prime Minister’s interaction was not as spontaneous as it appeared — a memo on his desk advised him on precisely what to discuss. The memo, labeled 'Call to Obama Thurs 14:55' and addressed to Cabinet members and the foreign policy team, instructed Cameron to raise issues including Congress, Iran, Syria, and the global economy — and to 'put down a marker' for a planned visit to Washington in May. The photograph also offered glimpses into Cameron’s daily routine. On his desk sat six pencils and only one pen — a subtle indicator that he is left-handed, as pencils prevent smudged ink. Next to the desk was a £160 Dolce Gusto Circolo coffee machine, alongside a framed photo of his wife, Samantha. Perched on a dado rail beside him was a bottle of Kiwi Premiere Shine Ultra Brilliant Shoe Polish, priced at £6.19 — evidence that, despite his privileged background, Cameron maintains personal, hands-on habits.

article_content: A 20-year-old man from Lowestoft, Suffolk, has been fined and banned from keeping animals after drinking two live goldfish as part of a viral social media challenge known as 'Neknomination'. Jack Blowers purchased the goldfish from a local pet shop in February with the explicit intent of consuming them — a plan captured on video by his friend Joseph Meikle. The footage, uploaded to Facebook, shows Blowers placing the fish in a pint glass filled with water, gravel, and fish food, then swallowing the entire mixture in one go. He subsequently vomited the contents into a toilet. Remarkably, the goldfish survived. Blowers retrieved them and placed them in his grandmother’s fishbowl, where they remain alive today, according to prosecutor Kevin Batch. The RSPCA pursued prosecution on grounds of premeditated cruelty, arguing the act caused unnecessary suffering and set a dangerous precedent. Although Blowers claimed he didn’t realize his actions were illegal, his defense highlighted a legal distinction: under UK law, the Animal Welfare Act 2006 protects vertebrates, meaning consuming invertebrates like octopuses would not constitute an offense — though this does not justify the act. Blowers pleaded guilty to two charges under the Animal Welfare Act 2006: failing to protect the fish from suffering and failing to meet their basic needs. The court heard evidence from a veterinarian confirming the fish endured significant distress. Joseph Meikle, who filmed the stunt, accepted a police caution in connection with the incident. Chair of the bench, Philip Key, fined Blowers £200 and ordered him to pay £600 in legal costs. He also imposed a 12-month ban on keeping any animals. In sentencing, Key stated: 'You bought two goldfish with the sole intention of drinking them and posting it online.' Outside court, Blowers admitted the stunt was 'stupid' and financially devastating. He added: 'I won’t do it again. My family are glad I didn’t do it with alcohol.' He confirmed he never named the fish but said he may visit them at his grandmother’s house.

Jack Blowers købte guldskallerne fra et lokalt dyrehandel i februar med det eksplicitte formål at spise dem — en plan fanget på video af hans ven Joseph Meikle. Videoen, uploadet til Facebook, viser Blowers, der placerer fiskene i et pints-glas fyldt med vand, kalk og fiskefoder, og så svælger hele blandingen i én slurk. Derefter kastede han indholdet ud i toilettet. Bemærkelsesværdigt nok overlevede guldskallerne. Blowers hentede dem og satte dem i sin bedstemors fiskeskar, hvor de lever endnu i dag, ifølge anklager Kevin Batch. RSPCA indledte en retssag på grundlag af forudtanke og grusomhed og argumenterede for, at handlingen forårsagede unødigt lidelse og skabte et farligt præcedens. Selv om Blowers påstod, at han ikke vidste, at hans handling var ulovlig, fremhævede hans forsvar en juridisk forskel: Ifølge britisk lov beskytter Dyrevelfærdloven 2006 ryggradsdyr, hvilket betyder, at at spise inverterater som blæksprutter ikke ville være ulovligt — selvom dette ikke retfærdiggør handlingen. Blowers indrømmede skyld i to krænkelser under Dyrevelfærdloven 2006: at ikke beskytte fiskene mod lidelse og ikke opfylde deres grundlæggende behov. Domstolen hørte bevis fra en dyrlæge, der bekræftede, at fiskene oplevede betydelig smerte. Joseph Meikle, der filmede stunts, accepterede en advarsel fra politiet i forbindelse med hændelsen. Formand for dommerpanel, Philip Key, bød Blowers 200 pund og pålagde ham at betale 600 pund i retsomkostninger. Han pålagde også et 12-måneds forbud mod at holde dyr. I dommen sagde Key: 'Du købte to guldskaller med det eneste formål at drikke dem og lade det blive til et indlæg på sociale medier.' Han bekræftede, at han aldrig har givet fiskene navne, men sagde, at han måske vil besøge dem hos sin bedstemor.

article_content: A hip Japanese café is offering customers a chance to create sweet, gummy replicas of themselves to give to someone they have a crush on — perfect for White Day on March 14. Located in Shibuya, Tokyo, the Fab Café is running a special two-session workshop for men who want to gift personalized gummy figures to their loved ones. For around £40 (6,000 yen), participants undergo a 3D body scan in a pose of their choice. The digital file is then used to 3D-print a mold, which is filled with gummy material during a follow-up session a week later. The event echoes a popular Valentine’s Day activity from last year, when women created chocolate face replicas to give to their partners. In Japan, Valentine’s Day is traditionally when women give chocolates — either 'honmei-choco' (for romantic interests) or 'giri-choco' (out of social obligation). On White Day, men return the gesture with gifts. Fab Café, which opened last year in trendy Shibuya, blends café culture with a maker space. It features 3D printers, a laser cutter, and other tools available to customers for a fee. The name plays on both 'fabulous' and 'fabrication'. Spaces for the gummy workshop are strictly limited due to the specialized equipment and hands-on nature of the process. Participants must attend both sessions: the first to be scanned, the second to pour and remove their gummy likeness. A post on the café’s website — translated via Google Translate — encourages guests: 'We’ve prepared a plan using high-spec 3D printers and scanners to create a full-body gummy version of you, capturing the same emotional impact as a chocolate face. Please express your feelings through a full-body gift.' Those in Tokyo can sign up via the café’s website.

article_content: Covered head to toe in padded protective gear, yet with his extremities still exposed, an Afghan bomb disposal expert risked his life to disarm a suicide bomber’s vest. Security forces in Jalalabad captured the attacker before he could detonate the device, restraining him to prevent activation. However, before the suspect could be transported for interrogation, the bomb squad was called in to safely disable the explosive device strapped to his chest. Dangerous work: A member of the Afghan bomb disposal unit approaches a captured suicide attacker to defuse the vest worn across his chest, in scenes reminiscent of the film The Hurt Locker. Armed only with wire cutters, the technician carefully disabled the improvised device. The suspect, his face bloodied and still bound by restraints, was then loaded onto a flatbed truck for transport to a detention center. Meanwhile, 100 miles away in Peshawar, Pakistan, a car bomb exploded as a convoy of paramilitary Frontier Corps troops passed through the city outskirts, killing at least 17 people and injuring dozens more. This was one of three coordinated attacks across Pakistan that day, claiming at least 43 lives — occurring just as UK Prime Minister David Cameron visited Islamabad, pledging support to combat extremism. In Quetta, the capital of Balochistan province, twin explosions near a Shiite mosque killed at least 22 people, including two women and several children, and wounded 65 others. According to police, a hand grenade was thrown first, causing panic and directing crowds toward the mosque, where a second suicide bomber detonated his device. No group has claimed responsibility, but suspicion has fallen on Lashkar-e-Jhangvi, a militant Sunni group known for targeting Shiites. In North Waziristan, a roadside bomb struck an army convoy, killing four soldiers and wounding 20. Intelligence officials say the Pakistani Taliban is the likely perpetrator, though no claim has been made. Scenes from the attacks show extensive damage to vehicles and shops, with rescue workers collecting evidence and emergency teams rushing to aid the injured. As the U.S.-led coalition negotiates its withdrawal from Afghanistan, the responsibility for countering such threats increasingly falls on Afghan security forces — a challenge that will only grow more urgent in the coming months.

Sikkerhedstropper fangede angriberen i Jalalabad, før han kunne udløse den, og bindede ham for at forhindre aktivering. Med kun et par trådklipper som våben, deaktiverede teknikeren forsigtigt den improviserede bombe. Mistænkte, med blodet på ansigtet og stadig bundet med reb, blev så ladet på en fladlastbil for at blive transporteret til et fængsel. Samtidigt, 100 kilometer væk i Peshawar, Pakistan, eksploderede en bilbombe, da et konvoj af paramilitære Frontier Corps-tropper passede gennem byens periferi og dræbte mindst 17 mennesker og sårede flere dusiner. Dette var en af tre koordinerede angreb i Pakistan den dag, der tog mindst 43 liv — og skete netop da den britiske premierminister David Cameron besøgte Islamabad og lovede støtte til bekæmpelse af ekstremisme. I Quetta, hovedstaden i provinsen Balochistan, udløste to eksplosioner nær en schiitisk moské og dræbte mindst 22 mennesker, herunder to kvinder og flere børn, samt sårede 65 andre. Ifølge politiet blev en håndgranat kastet først, hvilket forårsagede panik og ledte folk mod moskéen, hvor en anden selvmordsangriber udløste sin bombe. Ingen gruppe har taget ansvar, men mistanke falder på Lashkar-e-Jhangvi, en militante sunni-gruppe kendt for at rette angreb mod schiitter. I Nord-Waziristan eksploderede en vejbombe en armékonvoj og dræbte fire soldater og sårede 20 andre. Intelligensmyndigheder mener den pakistanske Taliban er den sandsynlige gerningsmand, selvom ingen har taget ansvar. Scener fra angrebet viser omfattende skader på biler og butikker, mens redningspersonale samler beviser og akutte team rækker hjælp til de sårede. Da den amerikanske-ledede koalition forhandler sine vilkår for tilbagetrækning fra Afghanistan, falder ansvaret for at håndtere sådanne trusler mere og mere på afghanske sikkerhedstropper — en udfordring, der kun vil blive mere presserende i de kommende måneder.

article_content: Mufid Elfgeeh, a 30-year-old Yemeni-American businessman and owner of Halal Mojo and Food Mart in Rochester, New York, was arrested after attempting to purchase two illegal firearm silencers from an FBI informant. Authorities allege he intended to use the weapons in targeted attacks against U.S. soldiers returning from Iraq and members of the Shiite Muslim community, motivated by extremist views tied to Syria’s conflict and support for Al-Qaeda. Court documents reveal that Elfgeeh had been under FBI surveillance since early last year. Investigators connected his personal computer to multiple Twitter accounts promoting jihadist rhetoric, calling Al-Qaeda 'our only savior' and urging donations for Sunni fighters in Syria. During a recorded conversation in December, Elfgeeh told the informant he was considering buying a large automatic weapon and ammunition, then going on a shooting spree — possibly wearing a vest and targeting people near their garages. Though he occasionally used the word 'we,' evidence suggests he planned to act alone and not immediately. The FBI supplied the informant with a Walther PPK .32-caliber pistol and a Glock 26, both fitted with working silencers, along with ammunition. Elfgeeh paid $1,050 for the items on Saturday and was taken into custody moments later. He now faces two charges for possessing unregistered silencers, each carrying a potential penalty of up to 10 years in prison and a $250,000 fine. At a Monday court hearing, Elfgeeh did not enter a plea. He was assigned a public defender and is currently held at Monroe County Jail. His bail hearing is set for June 16. Authorities say they have no indication he was part of an organized group — his plans appear to have been self-directed.

Myndighederne påstår, at han havde til hensigt at bruge våbnene til målrettede angreb mod amerikanske soldater, der vendte tilbage fra Irak, og medlemmer af det shiitiske muslimske fællesskab, motiveret af ekstremistiske holdninger forbundet med Syriens konflikt og støtte til Al-Qa'ida. Under et optaget samråd i december fortalte Elfgeeh informanten, at han overvejede at købe en stor automatisk pistol og ammunitionsforråd og så gå på et skydningssvær — muligvis med en vest og målrette folk nær deres garager. Han står nu ansvarlig for to anklager om besiddelse af ulovlige skyderdæmpere, hver med en potentielt straf på op til 10 års fængsel og en bøde på 250.000 dollar. Myndighederne siger, at de ikke har nogen indikation for, at han var en del af en organiseret gruppe — hans planer virker at være selvledede.

article_content: Not long ago, I rose to speak on the floor of the Texas State Senate, hoping that Republican lawmakers would hear how their latest healthcare proposal would harm women across the state. This bill would shut down nearly 90% of women’s clinics — leaving only five to serve millions. This follows the closure of more than 50 clinics after state funding was withdrawn, eliminating vital services like cancer screenings and birth control. With only five clinics remaining in a state as vast as Texas, countless women would face impossible barriers to care. Real Texans don’t want women to die from preventable cancers because they can’t reach a clinic. They don’t want women to lose control of their futures because contraception is out of reach. During the filibuster, women from every corner of Texas shared their stories: One said birth control let her choose when to become a mother. Another described how a clinic supported her through the heartbreak of losing a wanted pregnancy. A third found comfort when her baby was dying inside her. This ‘people’s filibuster’ became a defining moment — when everyday Texans stood up and said: enough. Enough of using Texas as a lab for extreme ideologies. Enough of enriching special interests while ignoring real needs. Enough of politicians deaf to the people they serve. Meanwhile, critical issues go unaddressed. In West, Texas, an unregulated fertilizer plant exploded on April 17, 2013, killing first responders who didn’t even know the dangers they faced — because there was no oversight. Real Texans believe in protecting each other — honoring parents, keeping children safe, and ensuring everyone has access to care. Yet Gov. Rick Perry and his allies refuse to expand healthcare, choosing political optics over people’s lives. They take pride in slashing education budgets: teacher layoffs, school closures, and the elimination of pre-K and arts programs — forcing districts to choose between basic subjects and early learning. Two years ago, I fought to protect our schools — and was punished by being removed from the Senate Education Committee. I’ve battled unfair redistricting meant to erase my district. Today, Texas Democrats are pushing for equal pay for equal work — essential for working families. But real Texans have never backed down from a fight. That’s what happened at the Capitol. We raised our voices. Now I ask Gov. Perry and the powerful leaders who’ve ignored us: Can you hear us now? And more importantly — are you listening?

Denne lov ville lukke næsten 90 % af kvindernes klinikker — og efterlade kun fem til at betjene millioner. Dette følger lukningen af mere end 50 klinikker, efter at statens finansiering blev trukket tilbage, hvilket fjernede vigtige tjenester som kræftscreening og fødselskontrol. Med kun fem klinikker tilbage i et så stort stat som Texas ville utallige kvinder stå over for umulige barrierer for behandling. Reelle texanere vil ikke, at kvinder dør af forhindrede kræftsygdomme, fordi de ikke kan nå en klinik. De vil ikke, at kvinder mister kontrol over deres fremtid, fordi kontraception er utilgængelig. Nok af at rige specialinteresser, mens man ignorerer reelle behov. Nok af politikere, der er døve for de mennesker, de skal repræsentere. Mens kritiske spørgsmål går ubehandlede. Reelle texanere tror på at tage vare på hinanden — at ære forældre, holde børnene sikre og sørge for, at alle har adgang til sundhed. Men guvernør Rick Perry og hans allierede nægter at udvide sundhedsvæsenet, og vælger politisk optik frem for menneskers liv. De er stolte af at skære i uddannelsesbudgetterne: lærere fyret, skoler lukket, og børnehave- og kunstprogrammer afskaffet — tvunget til at vælge mellem grundfag og tidlig undervisning. For to år siden kæmpede jeg for at beskytte vores skoler — og blev straffet ved at blive fjernet fra Uddannelsesudvalget. Jeg har kæmpet mod uretfærdig valgdistriktsgrenseændring, der skulle gøre mit distrikt forsvundet. I dag kæmper texanske demokrater for lige løn for lige arbejde — nødvendigt for arbejdende familier. Men reelle texanere har aldrig givet op i en kamp. Det skete på kapitoliet. Vi rejste vores stemmer. Nu spørger jeg guvernør Perry og de magtfulde ledere, der har ignoreret os: Kan I høre os nu? Og vigtigere — lytter I?

article_content: Official figures reveal that Gary Dobson and David Norris, the two men convicted of the 1993 racist murder of 18-year-old Stephen Lawrence, received a combined total of £425,655 in legal aid from taxpayers. Dobson, a drug trafficker, was awarded £199,109 for his trial and an additional £4,200 for his failed appeal — totaling £203,309. Norris, the son of a gangster, received £222,346 to defend himself against the murder charge; his appeal funding remains unconfirmed. The amounts far surpass the £320,000 compensation paid to Stephen’s parents, Doreen and Neville Lawrence, for police failures that delayed justice for two decades. The Crown Prosecution Service spent £287,056 prosecuting the case, led by counsel Timothy Roberts QC for Dobson and Stephen Batten QC for Norris. Convictions came after a six-week trial at the Old Bailey in January 2012, based largely on newly uncovered forensic evidence — including microscopic traces of blood, hair, and fibers from the suspects’ clothing — and a chilling surveillance video showing Norris expressing violent racist views and Dobson recounting threats against a Black colleague. Both men appealed their convictions: Dobson withdrew his challenge in March 2013; Norris’s appeal was rejected by the Court of Appeal in May 2013. The case remains open for three other suspects — brothers Neil and Jamie Acourt and their friend Luke Knight — who have never been prosecuted. The revelations emerged shortly after Justice Secretary Chris Grayling criticized legal aid spending as 'unsustainable,' noting the system costs £2 billion annually. A spokesperson for the Legal Aid Agency emphasized that legal aid is available to anyone facing serious criminal charges, subject to a means test — though it is unclear whether either defendant contributed financially to their own defense.
translated_content: Officielle tal viser, at Gary Dobson og David Norris, de to mænd, der blev dømt for det racemotiverede mord på den 18-årige Stephen Lawrence i 1993, fik en samlet sum på 425.655 pund i retshjælp fra skatteyderne. Dobson, en narkotikahandler, fik 199.109 pund til sin retssag og yderligere 4.200 pund til hans mislykkede appels — i alt 203.309 pund. Norris, søn af en ganger, fik 222.346 pund til at forsvare sig mod mordanklagen; hans appelfinansiering er endnu ikke bekræftet. Beløbene overstiger langt de 320.000 pund i erstatning, der blev betalt til Stephens forældre, Doreen og Neville Lawrence, for politiets fejl, der forsinkede retfærdighed i to årtier. Anklageriet brugte 287.056 pund til at anklage sagen, med Timothy Roberts QC som anklager for Dobson og Stephen Batten QC som forsvar for Norris. Dømmelserne kom efter en seks uger lang retssag ved Old Bailey i januar 2012, baseret hovedsagelig på nyligt opdagede forensiske beviser — herunder mikroskopiske spor af blod, hår og fibre fra mistænktes tøj — og en skræmmende overvågningsvideo, hvor Norris udtrykte voldelige racisterede holdninger og Dobson fortalte om trusler mod en sort kollega. Begge mænd anklagede deres domme: Dobson trak sin appels tilbage i marts 2013; Norris' appels blev afvist af Højesteretten i maj 2013. Sagen er stadig åben for tre andre mistænkte — brødrene Neil og Jamie Acourt og deres ven Luke Knight — som aldrig er blevet tiltalt. Opdagelsen kom kort efter, at justitsminister Chris Grayling kritiserede retshjælpsudgifterne som 'utilpas', og understregede, at systemet koster 2 milliarder pund årligt. En talesperson for Retshjælpsmyndigheden understregede, at retshjælp er tilgængelig for alle, der står for en alvorlig straffesag, underlagt en økonomisk vurdering — selvom det er ukendt, om nogen af de to tiltalte har bidraget finansielt til deres egen forsvaret.

article_content: It’s been nearly seven years since Fiona Apple last released an album, and fans have been patiently waiting — or settling for imitators like Lana Del Rey and Paz de la Huerta. Now, the enigmatic singer-songwriter is back, and she’s not coming quietly. Her upcoming fourth studio record carries a title so sprawling it reads like a philosophical manifesto: 'The Idler Wheel is wiser than the Driver of the Screw, and Whipping Cords will serve you more than Ropes will ever do.' Though it’s 67 words shorter than her previous record’s title, it still stretches across 23 words, each one deliberately capitalized as if to force you to pause and ponder. No official release date has been announced, but whispers point to June. The real challenge? Figuring out what to call it. Most will likely shorten it to 'The Idler Wheel,' but technically, you could also refer to it as 'Driver of the Screw,' 'Whipping Cords,' or even 'Serve You More.' Someone at Epic Records is probably already dreading the task of crafting social media posts with the absurdly long hashtag: #theidlerwheeliswiserthanthedriverofthescrewandwhippingcordswillserveyoumorethanropeswilleverdo. Whether you find it brilliant or baffling, one thing’s certain: Fiona Apple still does things her own way.
translated_content: Det er næsten syv år siden Fiona Apple sidst udgav et album, og fans har ventet tålmodigt — eller tilpasset sig efterligninger som Lana Del Rey og Paz de la Huerta. Nu er den mystiske sangerinde tilbage, og hun kommer ikke stille. Hendes kommende fjerde studiealbum bærer et titel, der læses som en filosofisk manifest: 'The Idler Wheel is wiser than the Driver of the Screw, and Whipping Cords will serve you more than Ropes will ever do.' Selvom det er 67 ord kortere end hendes tidligere albums titel, strækker det sig stadig over 23 ord, hvert enkelt bevidst storbogstaveret, som for at tvinge dig til at standse og tænke. Ingen officiel udgivelsesdato er annonceret, men rygterne peger på juni. Den virkelige udfordring? At finde ud af, hvad man skal kalde det. De fleste vil sandsynligvis forkorte det til 'The Idler Wheel,' men teknisk set kunne du også referere til det som 'Driver of the Screw,' 'Whipping Cords' eller endda 'Serve You More.' Nogen hos Epic Records er sandsynligvis allerede ved at frygte opgaven med at skabe sociale medieindlæg med den absurd lange hashtag: #theidlerwheeliswiserthanthedriverofthescrewandwhippingcordswillserveyoumorethanropeswilleverdo. Uanset om du finder det genialt eller forvirrende, én ting er sikker: Fiona Apple gør stadig ting på sin egen måde.

article_content: Steph and Dom Parker — the beloved 'posh couple' from Channel 4’s Gogglebox — are putting their historic Grade I listed home, The Salutation, on the market for £3.5 million. Located in Sandwich, Kent, the 16-bedroom estate was designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens, the architect behind the Cenotaph and Britain’s embassy in Washington, D.C. Its interiors, featuring a cream chintz sofa, gold-trimmed drinks table, and oak piano, have become iconic thanks to the couple’s drunkenly charming TV commentary. Since buying the property in 2004, the Parkers have transformed it into one of Kent’s most luxurious B&Bs, offering guests a refined experience described on their website as 'like a fine claret leaving you with a rounded after-taste'. Surrounded by 3.5 acres of meticulously landscaped gardens — designed by legendary horticulturist Gertrude Jekyll — the estate includes a main house, secondary residence, coach house, gardener’s cottage, and gatehouse. Outdoors, visitors find a tropical garden, kitchen plot, lake, and vegetable patch, all tucked behind stone walls and mature trees for complete privacy. The property also boasts seven reception rooms, 14 bathrooms, marble countertops, and cream-painted walls — all preserved with care. The Parkers, who met in 1998 and have two young children and a sausage dog named Gigi, originally worked in property management before rising to fame. article_content: At just 13 years old, Dominique was trafficked for sex — one of an estimated 100,000 American children exploited annually, according to the anti-trafficking nonprofit Saving Innocence. Now 18 and back in school, she is far from alone. As Mark Harris, director of the powerful new film Abducted, explains, teenage girls are especially vulnerable to traffickers who prey on dreams of stardom. 'Many girls arrive in Los Angeles hoping to become pop stars, only to be drugged and trapped in trafficking networks,' he says. 'Only about 2% ever land real work. Agents don’t care about talent — only profit.' Harris’s investigation into LA’s hidden underbelly uncovered disturbing truths: child abduction, sexual exploitation, rape, and systematic coercion. These realities became the foundation for Abducted — a raw, unflinching film that shatters Hollywood’s glossy image. 'I spent a night in Hollywood with Saving Innocence,' Harris recalls. 'In just hours, I encountered child sexual abuse, abduction, trafficking, and two girls snatched off the street.' He adds: 'People called the film controversial because it’s dark — but I wanted to go as close to the truth as possible. I refused to make a fairy tale. I wanted viewers to see what Hollywood really hides.' Harris and Saving Innocence insist every scene in Abducted is rooted in real events — a claim reinforced by survivors like Dominique and Keila McCain. Keila, now in her twenties, was trafficked starting at age 12. 'By 18, it was my last arrest for prostitution,' she says. 'I spent six years trapped — but that doesn’t define me.' She met her trafficker at 15, when he approached her on the street. 'He noticed I wouldn’t make eye contact and assumed I had a pimp. When I admitted I didn’t, he asked what I was doing out there. That’s how it started.' For years, Keila and other girls were forced to work every night, moved across state lines to evade detection. Today, Keila lives independently, thanks to Saving Innocence. 'A year ago, I could only see the streets. Now, I feel worthy of love. My past doesn’t erase my present.' Abducted releases March 17. Learn more at savinginnocence.org.
translated_content: På blot 13 år blev Dominique menneskehandlet til seksuelle formål – en af de anslåede 100.000 amerikanske børn, der udbydes hvert år, ifølge den antihandlingsorganisation Saving Innocence. Nu 18 og tilbage i skole, er hun langt fra alene. Som Mark Harris, instruktør af den kraftfulde nye film Abducted, forklarer, er teenagepiger særligt sårbare over for menneskehandlere, der udnytter drømme om stardom. 'Mange piger kommer til Los Angeles med håb om at blive popstjerner, men bliver drænet og fanget i menneskehandelsnetværk,' siger han. 'Kun cirka 2 % finder et rigtigt job. Agenterne bryder sig ikke om talent – kun om penge.' Harris’ undersøgelse af LA’s skjulte underverden afslørede skræmmende sandheder: børnefængsling, seksuel udbydelse, voldtegt og systematisk tvang. Disse realiteter blev grundlaget for Abducted – en rå, ubarmhjertig film, der knuser Hollywoods glansbillede. 'Jeg tilbragte en nat i Hollywood med Saving Innocence,' husker Harris. 'I blot få timer mødte jeg børnesexuelt misbrug, fængsling, menneskehandling og to piger, der blev taget fra gaden.' Han tilføjer: 'Mennesker kaldte filmen kontroversiel, fordi den er mørk – men jeg ville gå så tæt på sandheden som muligt. Jeg nægtede at lave et eventyr. Jeg ønskede, at seerne skulle se, hvad Hollywood virkelig gemmer.' Harris og Saving Innocence påstår, at hver scene i Abducted er baseret på virkelige begivenheder – en påstand understøttet af overleverne Dominique og Keila McCain. Keila, nu i tyveårene, blev menneskehandlet fra alderen 12. 'Ved 18 var det min sidste arrestering for prostitution,' siger hun. 'Jeg tilbragte seks år fanget – men det definerer ikke mig.' Hun mødte sin menneskehandler ved 15, da han nærmede sig hende på gaden. 'Han bemærkede, at jeg ikke så ham i øjnene, og antog, at jeg havde en pimp. Da jeg sagde nej, spurgte han, hvad jeg gjorde derude. Så startede det.' I årevis blev Keila og andre piger tvunget til at arbejde hver nat, flyttet mellem stater for at undgå opdagelse. I dag bor Keila uafhængigt takket være Saving Innocence. 'For et år siden kunne jeg kun se gaderne. Nu føler jeg mig værdig af kærlighed. Min fortid ændrer ikke mit nutid.' Abducted udkommer den 17. marts. Lær mere på savinginnocence.org.

article_content: Better late than never — Patrick Dempsey, beloved by millions as McDreamy from Grey’s Anatomy, has officially been named People’s Sexiest Man Alive at age 57. 'I’m glad this is happening now,' the actor told the magazine. 'It’s wonderful to be recognized, and yes, my ego enjoys the boost — but more importantly, it gives me a platform to do something meaningful.' When first informed he’d be the next cover star, Dempsey recalled, 'I was completely shocked — then I laughed. Is this a joke? I’ve always been the bridesmaid!' He admitted he’d long since stopped imagining such an honor. 'My ego is happy,' he said. Though he departed Grey’s Anatomy in 2015, Dempsey returned briefly as McDreamy in a 2021 cameo. Now, he’s taking on a new challenge: portraying legendary Italian F1 driver Piero Taruffi in Michael Mann’s upcoming film, Ferrari. To embody the role, he dyed his hair stark white — a look that stunned fans at last year’s D23 Expo. A passionate racing enthusiast in real life, Dempsey told Deadline at the Venice Film Festival that he aggressively pursued the part, calling the script 'the best I’ve ever read in the motorsport world.'

article_content: At the Fei Yan Acrobatics Troupe in Hunan Province, China, children begin grueling training as young as eight, dedicating nearly the entire day to perfecting acrobatic stunts. With sessions from 8:10 a.m. to 11:30 a.m. and 2:00 p.m. to 5:30 p.m., and only 90 minutes off daily, their lives revolve around discipline, endurance, and precision. Led by 76-year-old Han Keting — a former state acrobat who once performed for Chairman Mao — the troupe operates with military-like rigor. Talent alone isn’t enough; unwavering commitment is mandatory. In early 2013, two children were dismissed for not training hard enough, a move Keting justified by saying, 'They could set bad examples.' Trainees live together in dormitories, forming deep bonds while mastering demanding routines like the 'Boneless Girl' — a feat where an acrobat places her chin on the floor and curls her body backward until her feet rest near her face. Every movement is repeated hundreds of times until flawless. Monthly progressions introduce even more difficult stunts, pushing young bodies to their limits. Han explains that acrobats have just five peak years — between ages 16 and 20 — after which physical stiffness and declining flexibility end careers. 'No one can perform my program anymore,' he says, 'it takes years of extremely hard training.' Although training is free and students wear patched shoes reflecting limited resources, those who earn a place in the troupe receive a professional contract and a steady monthly wage. Since its founding, the Fei Yan Acrobatics Troupe has toured globally — from Britain and the United States to Germany, Mexico, and Thailand — earning international acclaim for its artistry and athleticism.

Med øvelser fra kl. 8.10 til 11.30 og fra 14.00 til 17.30 og kun 90 minutters pause om dagen, handler deres liv om disciplin, udholdenhed og præcision. Lejet af den 76-årige Han Keting — en tidligere statsakrobat, der engang optrådte for formanden Mao — opererer truppen med militær nøjagtighed. Talent alene er ikke nok; ubønhørlig engagement er påkrævet. I begyndelsen af 2013 blev to børn afskediget for ikke at træne hårdt nok, en handling, som Keting begrundede med: 'De kunne give et dårligt eksempel.' Uddannelsesstuderende bor sammen i sovesale og danner tætte bånd, mens de mestrer krævende numre som 'Den benløse pige' — et trick, hvor en akrobat sætter hagen på gulvet og bøjer kroppen bagud, indtil fødderne ligger nær ansigtet. Hvert enkelt bevægelse gentages hundreder af gange, indtil den er fejlfri. Månedlige fremskridt introducerer endnu sværere numre og presser unge kroppe til deres grænser. Han forklarer, at akrobater har kun fem topår — mellem 16 og 20 år — efter hvilke fysisk stivhed og formindsket fleksibilitet afslutter karrieren. 'Ingen kan udføre mit program længere,' siger han, 'det kræver år af yderst hård træning.' Selvom uddannelse er gratis og børnene bærer flækkede sko, som spejler begrænsede ressourcer, får de, der får plads i truppen, en professionel kontrakt og en fast månedlig løn. Siden dens oprettelse har Fei Yan Akrobat-truppen turneret verden over — fra Storbritannien og USA til Tyskland, Mexico og Thailand — og har opnået international anerkendelse for sin kunstneriske og athletiske ydeevne.

article_content: The number of Arsenal players injured during the international break has risen to four following Tomas Rosicky’s setback in the Czech Republic’s Euro qualifier against Turkey on Friday night. Rosicky, who had already missed Monday’s match against Kazakhstan, said: 'I couldn’t make any sharp movements or sprint. If I tried to play at full intensity, I wouldn’t help the team. I’ll head back to London and see what the doctors say. They’ve noted some swelling between the muscles.' The 34-year-old midfielder becomes the fourth Arsenal player to suffer an injury while on international duty. He was seen playing against Chelsea earlier in the season. Mesut Özil is sidelined for three months after sustaining a knee ligament injury during Germany’s training session. Laurent Koscielny was sent home from France’s camp due to tendinitis. Meanwhile, Danny Welbeck — signed from Manchester United for £16 million on transfer deadline day — suffered a minor ankle knock during England’s 1-0 victory over Estonia in Tallinn on Sunday. He is expected to resume training with Arsenal on Wednesday.

article_content: The International Criminal Court (ICC) has postponed the start of Kenyan President Uhuru Kenyatta’s trial on charges of crimes against humanity by three months, now set for February 5. The decision follows a defense request for additional time to prepare, which the prosecution acknowledged as reasonable. Originally scheduled for November 12, the trial will proceed at the ICC’s seat in The Hague, Netherlands. Kenyatta faces five counts of crimes against humanity tied to deadly ethnic violence following the disputed December 2007 presidential election. After then-President Mwai Kibaki was declared winner, clashes erupted, leaving more than 1,000 dead and hundreds of thousands displaced. Prosecutors allege Kenyatta funded a local militia responsible for retaliatory attacks against communities supporting opposition candidates. Deputy President William Ruto and radio presenter Joshua arap Sang are also charged in connection with the same events. Ruto and Sang’s trial began in September. Both Kenyatta and Ruto have consistently denied orchestrating violence along ethnic lines. The African Union has criticized the ICC for targeting sitting African leaders, urging delays in such cases. Meanwhile, Kenya’s parliament voted in September to withdraw from the ICC’s jurisdiction — though the process requires formal notification to the United Nations and will take time to finalize. The ICC confirmed the trials will continue regardless. Although exempted from attending most proceedings, Kenyatta must appear at the opening and closing statements. He has stated his willingness to cooperate fully with the court to clear his name. Kenya’s previous government abandoned a domestic tribunal agreement, prompting the ICC’s intervention. Kenya is only the second African nation — after Sudan — to have a sitting president face ICC charges. Sudan’s Omar al-Bashir, wanted for war crimes, has largely ignored his ICC warrant.
translated_content: Den Internationale Strafdomstol (ICC) har udskydt begyndelsen af den kenyanske præsidents Uhuru Kenyattas retssag om forbrydelser mod menneskeheden med tre måneder, så den nu er sat til den 5. februar. Beslutningen følger en anmodning fra forsvarerne om mere tid til forberedelse, hvilket anklagemyndigheden anerkendte som rimeligt. Retssagen var oprindelig planlagt til den 12. november og vil finde sted på ICCs hovedkvarter i Den Haag, Nederlandene. Kenyatta står anklaget for fem punkter af forbrydelser mod menneskeheden i forbindelse med dødelig etnisk vold efter det omdiskuterede præsidentvalg i december 2007. Efter at den daværende præsident Mwai Kibaki blev erklæret vinder, udsprang voldelige sammenstød, hvor over 1.000 mennesker blev dræbt og hundreder af tusinder blev fordrevet. Anklagerne påstår, at Kenyatta finansierede en lokal milits, der udførte hævnangreb mod samfund, der støttede oppositionskandidater. Vicepræsident William Ruto og radiomoderen Joshua arap Sang er også anklaget i forbindelse med de samme begivenheder. Rutos og Sangs retssag startede i september. Både Kenyatta og Ruto har konsekvent afvist, at de har koordineret vold langs etniske linjer. Den Afrikanske Union har kritiseret ICC for at rette fokus mod sidstegende afrikanske ledere og opfordret til at udskyde sådanne sager. Imens har det kenyanske parlament stemt i september for at trække sig ud af ICCs jurisdiktion — selvom processen kræver en formel meddelelse til FN og vil tage tid at gennemføre. ICC bekræftede, at retssagene vil fortsætte uanset dette. Selvom han er fritaget for at deltage i de fleste forhandlinger, skal Kenyatta være til stede ved åbningen og afslutningen. Han har erklæret sit ønske om at samarbejde fuldt ud med domstolen for at renske sit navn. Den tidligere kenyanske regering brød en aftale om at etablere en særlig domstol til at dømme mistænkte i den eftervalgsvold, hvilket fik ICC til at træde ind. Kenya er det andet afrikanske land — efter Sudan — hvor en sidstegende præsident står anklaget ved ICC. Sudans Omar al-Bashir, der er ejet af en ICC-arrestordre for krigsforbrydelser, har i stor grad ignoreret sin arrestordre.

article_content: Hundreds of law enforcement officers continued a frantic search on Saturday for Eric Matthew Frein, the suspect in the fatal shooting of Pennsylvania State Trooper Cpl. Byron Dickson. The manhunt intensified hours after authorities reported bursts of gunfire near Frein’s family home in the Poconos Mountains — an area not far from Canadensis, Pennsylvania. Ralph Megliola, chairman of Barrett Township’s board of supervisors, confirmed that up to 400 officers — including personnel from the U.S. Marshals Service, the ATF, and the FBI — were involved in the operation. Although police had surrounded an area believed to harbor Frein on Friday night, there have been no credible sightings since then. State police issued repeated warnings for residents in Price and Barrett townships to stay indoors, avoid windows, and refrain from traveling to the region. Authorities did not confirm whether Frein was definitively surrounded but acknowledged exchanging gunfire with a suspect matching his description. Frein, 31, is accused of ambushing Dickson on September 12 outside the state police barracks in Blooming Grove and wounding another officer. The FBI has placed him on its Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list and is offering a $100,000 reward for information leading to his arrest. Officials describe Frein as a survivalist with deep knowledge of firearms and a longstanding animosity toward law enforcement. He reportedly shaved his head on the sides with long hair on top — a style broader than a traditional mohawk — and was active in a military simulation group that staged Cold War-era reenactments using Airsoft guns. State Police Commissioner Frank Noonan stated investigators have evidence Frein openly expressed intentions to kill police officers and carry out mass violence. Lt. Col. George Bivens emphasized Frein’s apparent fascination with Eastern European military history and attire. In a direct message to Frein, Bivens declared: 'If you are cowering in some cool, damp place... we are coming for you. It is only a matter of time until we bring you to justice.' Frein’s FBI wanted poster notes he is a heavy smoker, a weapons enthusiast, and claims to have fought alongside Serbians in Africa and studied Russian and Serbian languages — assertions that remain unverified.

article_content: As the old saying goes, 'keep your friends close and your enemies closer' — but this cricket took it literally. Perched calmly on the head of a green papua tree frog, its natural predator, the insect appeared undisturbed while the amphibian rested nearby. The scene unfolded on a red petal in photographer Monica Anantyowati’s backyard in Malang, East Java, Indonesia. The cricket crawled slowly across the flower, brushing against the frog’s body and eventually settling on its head — mere inches from its mouth. Typically, such an encounter would end in the cricket being consumed. But instead, both animals remained still for an extended period, seemingly at ease with one another. The frog did not strike; the cricket did not flee. Green papua tree frogs are native to northern and eastern Australia, Papua New Guinea, and parts of Indonesia. They thrive in swampy, humid habitats and are not endangered, though they are frequently preyed upon by domestic cats and dogs. In Indonesia alone, an estimated 75,000 are exported annually as exotic pets. Anantyowati, 42, described the moment as surreal. 'I was shocked — usually, the frog would eat the cricket in seconds. But they just sat there, quietly together. It felt like they’d made an unspoken truce.' She rushed to grab her camera, returning moments later to find the pair still in place — peaceful, undisturbed. 'Nature doesn’t always follow the rules we expect,' she said. 'That’s why I love photography — it reveals mysteries the naked eye can’t see.' The images have since gone viral, prompting questions about whether the frog was satiated, distracted, or simply not triggered to hunt. While scientists caution against attributing human-like intentions to the animals, the moment remains a powerful reminder of nature’s unpredictability.

Sideløbende roligt på hovedet af en grøn papuansk træfrø, dens naturlige byttedyr, virkede insektet uforstyrret, mens amfibiet hvilede nær ved. Scenen fandt sted på et rødt blad i fotografens baghave i Malang, Øst-Java, Indonesien. Græshoppen kravlede langsomt over bladet, berørte kroppen på frøen og satte sig endelig på dens hoved — kun få tomme inches fra dens mund. Normalt ville sådan en situation ende med, at græshoppen blev spist. Men i stedet forblev begge dyr stille i længere tid, som om de var i fred med hinanden. Frøen angreb ikke; græshoppen løb ikke væk. Grønne papuanske træfrø findes i nordlige og østlige Australien, Papua Ny Guinea og dele af Indonesien. De trives i sumpede, fugtige områder og er ikke truede, selvom de ofte bliver ædt af huse og hunde. I Indonesien eksporteres der årligt op til 75.000 eksemplarer som eksotiske husdyr. Anantyowati, 42, beskrev øjeblikket som surrealt. 'Jeg var chokeret — normalt ville frøen spise græshoppen i sekunder. Men de sad bare der, stille sammen. 'Naturen følger ikke altid de regler, vi forventer,' sagde hun. 'Det er derfor jeg elsker fotografering — den afslører mysterier, det blotte øje ikke kan se.' Billederne har siden gået viral og har vækket spørgsmål om, om frøen var mæt, distraheret eller simpelthen ikke udløst til at jage. Selvom videnskabsfolk advarede mod at tilskrive dyrene menneskelige intentioner, er øjeblikket en kraftig påmindelse om naturens uhåndterbarhed.

article_content: Jackie Chan, the global kung fu icon, has publicly taken accountability for his son Jaycee Chan’s recent drug arrest in Beijing. On August 14, police raided an apartment in the Dongcheng district and found both Jaycee — a 32-year-old Hong Kong-born actor — and 23-year-old Taiwanese actor Kai Ko in possession of marijuana. According to state media, over 100 grams of the substance were discovered in Jaycee’s home, and he was additionally charged with allowing others to use drugs there. In a heartfelt post on Weibo, where he has over 23 million followers, Jackie Chan described feeling ‘extremely furious’ and ‘shocked,’ adding that Jaycee’s mother is devastated. He urged young fans to view his son’s situation as a warning, saying, ‘I failed to guide him properly — and I share the blame.’ He and Jaycee bowed in apology to the public. Meanwhile, Kai Ko appeared on CCTV, visibly emotional, admitting he’d set a terrible example and sincerely apologized to everyone who supported him. Their arrests come amid a sweeping national campaign targeting drug use in China’s entertainment sector, with over 7,000 individuals detained since January — a 72% spike from last year. Other celebrities, including actor Zhang Mo and singer Li Daimo, have also faced penalties, the latter receiving a nine-month sentence for hosting a crystal meth party. In response, major talent agencies have pledged to ban drug use entirely and terminate contracts with any artist who violates the law.

article_content: By David Wilkes. Created: 08:26 EST, 6 February 2014. With its palatial interior, grand Elizabethan features, and rustic views over the Malvern Hills, Sabina Carter’s £1.25 million apartment embodied good taste and propriety — unfortunately, the same could not be said for its owner. After a heated dispute with a wealthy neighbor in the 17th-century stately home, Carter sent an email telling her to 'go hang yourself.' Carter, a 50-year-old divorcee, was evicted from Westwood House after sending what the court described as a 'disturbing and distressing' email to Janice Brookes, chair of the residents’ committee. The court heard that Carter had defaulted on £11,000 in service charges for the upkeep of the Grade I-listed building and its grounds. Westwood House, located in the countryside near Droitwich in Worcestershire, consists of 12 luxury flats, each subject to monthly service fees. Prosecutor Jackie Rogers stated that Carter, who was declared bankrupt in 2010, had long struggled to maintain harmonious relations with neighbors. In September 2012, she received a formal harassment warning ordering her to have no contact with Mrs. Brookes. Yet in November of the previous year, the former Lufthansa air hostess sent Brookes — a jeweler — an obscene email containing the line: 'My only other suggestion is that you go and hang yourself, but with your low IQ, you couldn’t manage that either.' The property — featuring an Elizabethan salon with 24-foot-high ceilings, a kitchen, and two bedrooms — was listed for sale at £1.25 million but remained unsold. Carter pleaded guilty at Worcester Magistrates’ Court to sending an email of a grossly offensive, indecent, or menacing character. In a victim impact statement, 48-year-old Mrs. Brookes described the message as 'distressing and disgusting.' Carter was given a 12-month conditional discharge, ordered to pay £250 in compensation to Mrs. Brookes, plus £85 in court costs and a £15 victim surcharge. Her defense lawyer, Paul Nicholls, said Carter had been under significant stress and was facing eviction due to mortgage default. He added: 'It is not a nice email. She wrote like a 15-year-old, not a 50-year-old. Things have settled down now.' Carter’s eviction marks the end of her dream of living in Westwood House’s opulent setting. Accessed via a three-quarter-mile private drive, the house was built by the Packington family, who rose to prominence under Henry VIII. When Carter purchased her 3,000-square-foot, two-bedroom flat in 1999 for £237,000, it was dilapidated — and she invested thousands restoring it. Even so, the property already featured impressive original elements: plasterwork dating to Elizabeth I’s reign and a ceiling gifted by Charles II in recognition of the Packingtons’ loyalty during the Civil War. Carter struggled to afford the flat’s annual running costs of approximately £4,000 — including £120 monthly service charges and £2,000 council tax. She listed the flat for sale in 2009. In an interview with the Mail on Sunday, Carter — who earned a living selling English luxury goods to German supermarkets — said: 'I want the money. And I want to downsize to somewhere more cozy and less grand.' The piece included a photo of her seated on a white sofa in the salon with her young children. But she failed to find a buyer and eventually remortgaged the property before declaring bankruptcy. Neighbors expressed relief at her departure. One said: 'She was a nightmare. People here have certain lifestyle expectations — she couldn’t accept that her personal circumstances meant she was living beyond her means.' Jacqueline Pointon, 69, who has lived in the house since 1953, said: 'People are relieved she has finally gone. The flat is empty now.' Another former neighbor suggested residents might celebrate her departure with a party — one she would certainly not be invited to. Carter now plans to return to Germany, where her mother is undergoing chemotherapy, the court heard. Mrs. Brookes was on holiday in Barbados and unavailable for comment.

Hun skrev som en 15-årig, ikke en 50-årig. Ting har nu sluppet ned.' Carters udvisning markerer slutningen på hendes drøm om at bo i Westwood Houses luksuriøse omgivelser. Tilgængelig via en tre-kvart-mil privat vej, blev huset bygget af Packington-familien, der steg frem under Henrik VIII. Carter havde svært ved at betale de årlige driftsomkostninger på cirka 4.000 pund — herunder 120 pund i månedlige servicegebyrer og 2.000 pund i kommunale afgifter. Folk her har visse forventninger til livsstil — hun kunne ikke acceptere, at hendes personlige omstændigheder betød, at hun boede uden for sine midler.' Jacqueline Pointon, 69, der har boet i huset siden 1953, da hendes far købte en af de første lejligheder, sagde: 'Alle er lettet over, at hun endelig er gået. Lejligheden er tom nu.' En anden tidligere nabo foreslog, at beboerne måske fejrede hendes afrejse med en fest — en hun sikkert ikke var inviteret til. article_content: Busch Gardens has removed headless props from this year's Howl-O-Scream Halloween attraction after complaints that the decapitated heads resembled beheadings carried out by the terrorist group ISIS. The change followed the release of graphic videos showing the murders of American journalists James Foley and Steven Sotloff, and British aid worker David Haines. Spokespeople for Busch Gardens in Virginia and Tampa stated that, given the recent events, some props may have unintentionally appeared insensitive and would no longer be featured in this year’s event. 'Many of the scenes in Busch Gardens' Howl-O-Scream are graphic in nature, but they are fictional and not intended to comment on current world events,' said spokesman Travis Claytor. 'The props were designed and purchased several months ago.' Complaints emerged in Williamsburg after the Virginia Gazette published a photo of five severed-head props from the Cut Throat Cove attraction — a pirate-themed haunted house featuring body parts and decapitated figures. The attraction’s website described the scene: 'Within this macabre market, the pirates have been slaughtered and mutiny is afoot. The way out lies with the buried treasure — and the blood-curdling screams you hear just might be your own.' Some visitors supported the removal. 'That’s not consistent with the Halloween spirit at all,' said parkgoer Hartley Bond to WAVY. 'I think it was good that they pulled it. It was out of order and insensitive to public sentiment. I'm glad they responded.' Others disagreed. 'It’s Halloween. I wouldn’t associate the two,' said Norman England. 'People go there for the scariness. What’s happening in the Middle East is entirely different.' The Virginia Gazette ran the photo on its front page three hours after media outlets reported ISIS had released a new video claiming responsibility for Haines’ killing. Editor Rusty Carter defended the decision: 'The photo was taken last week as part of a preview assignment. The figures are cartoonish and not realistic. It is the job of journalists to report the news — not censor it.' Busch Gardens Williamsburg’s Halloween attraction opened in mid-September; the Tampa location’s opens on September 26.

Ændringen fulgte efter udgivelsen af grafiske videoer, der viste mordene på de amerikanske journalister James Foley og Steven Sotloff, samt den britiske hjælper David Haines. Talsmænd for Busch Gardens i Virginia og Tampa sagde, at i lyset af de seneste begivenheder kunne nogle rekvirer være uønsket blevet opfattet som følelsesløse og vil ikke længere være en del af dette års Howl-O-Scream. 'Mange af scenerne i Busch Gardens' Howl-O-Scream er grafiske i natur, men de er fiktive og ikke beregnet til at kommentere på aktuelle verdensbegivenheder,' sagde talsmand Travis Claytor. 'Rekvirerne blev designet og købt for flere måneder siden.'
