article_content: In a move that left many in Britain stunned, the United States publicly singled out France as its 'oldest ally' during a joint announcement of potential military action against Syria — while making no reference to the UK, despite decades of close cooperation. As Secretary of State John Kerry spoke from the White House, he praised France, Australia, and Turkey for standing with the US, emphasizing that the West could not ignore the use of chemical weapons. He cited thousands of reports confirming that the Syrian government had killed 1,429 civilians, including 426 children, in a nerve agent attack near Damascus. Kerry warned that failing to respond would invite history’s harshest judgment, framing the potential strike as a moral duty, not merely a strategic one. President Obama echoed this sentiment, stating the US preferred coordinated global action but would not allow paralysis to dictate its response. His remark that 'many think something should be done, but nobody wants to do it' was widely interpreted as a quiet rebuke to Britain, whose Parliament had just voted down participation in any military operation. The UK’s absence from the coalition was particularly painful given that British forces had been preparing for deployment. Defence Secretary Philip Hammond admitted it was 'deeply uncomfortable' to watch allies act without Britain, calling it a blow to national pride and military readiness. Back in London, the political fallout was intense. Prime Minister David Cameron faced fierce criticism from both sides of the aisle after his rushed parliamentary vote failed to secure support. Thirty Conservative MPs joined Labour in rejecting even the principle of intervention, while another 32 were absent — including ten from his own cabinet. Cameron accused Labour leader Ed Miliband of siding with Russia, while Miliband countered that Britain couldn’t simply turn away from suffering civilians. Foreign Secretary William Hague reportedly felt 'deeply depressed,' and former Liberal Democrat leader Lord Ashdown described the moment as the most shameful of his lifelong public service. The vote marked the first time since the 18th century that a British prime minister had lost a parliamentary motion on military action. Chancellor George Osborne urged the nation to engage in deep reflection about Britain’s global role. Meanwhile, protesters in Syria held signs demanding international intervention, and UN investigators collected soil samples near suspected missile debris in the Damascus suburbs. Though the US stressed the strikes would be 'limited and narrow' with no ground troops, the message was clear: Washington was ready to act — and Britain, for now, was not.

article_content: Women hold only 15% of executive positions in Fortune 500 companies — a figure that remains stubbornly low. Last month, Rashida Manjoo, the United Nations Special Rapporteur on Violence Against Women, labeled the UK’s workplace culture as uniquely entrenched in sexism, describing it as a 'boys' club' more pervasive than in any other nation. Psychologists suggest a hidden barrier to progress: many men identify as supporters of gender equality — 'secret feminists' — yet remain silent, fearing their intentions will be misunderstood or dismissed. Adam Grant, a professor of psychology at the University of Pennsylvania, notes that male voices are conspicuously absent in conversations about women’s leadership. Among prominent books on women and business, male authors are underrepresented. In an article for The Atlantic, Grant explains that some men want to advocate for women but hesitate, believing their lack of personal stake in the issue makes their support seem insincere. 'There’s evidence that when a cause seems inconsistent with our self-interest, we fear that we’ll incur a backlash, so we hold back,' he writes. But is this silence merely an excuse? Grant says no. Research supports the idea that men face social costs when they champion women’s advancement — even when their motives are pure. A study from the University of Auckland tested the Ambivalent Sexism Theory, which divides prejudice against women into two forms: hostile sexism — overt hostility or belief in female inferiority — and benevolent sexism — the paternalistic view that women need protection and care. The study found that women with a stronger sense of entitlement were more likely to endorse statements like 'Women should be cherished and protected by men.' Separate research by psychologists Rebecca Ratner (University of Maryland) and Dale Miller (Stanford) revealed that when men openly supported women’s rights, both men and women reacted with surprise — even hostility. In one experiment, participants were less willing to support a fictional policy benefiting the opposite sex, despite showing equal opposition to policies affecting their own gender. Grant recounts a real-life example: when a man voiced support for increasing women in leadership during a workshop, his female colleagues responded not with gratitude, but with suspicion — questioning whether he was seeking romantic advantage. Grant argues that advancing gender equity requires more than breaking glass ceilings — it demands dismantling the fear that prevents men from becoming active allies. 'Secret male feminists' must be encouraged to speak up, not silenced by doubt or social risk.

Psykologer foreslår en skjult barriere for fremskridt: mange mænd identificerer sig som støttere af kønslig ligestilling — 'hemmelige feminister' — men holder sig tavse af frygt for, at deres hensigter vil blive misforstået eller afvist. Adam Grant, professor i psykologi ved University of Pennsylvania, bemærker, at mandlige stemmer er tydeligt fraværende i samtaler om kvinders ledelse. Blandt fremtrædende bøger om kvinder og forretning er mandlige forfattere underrepræsenterede. I en artikel i The Atlantic forklarer Grant, at nogle mænd ønsker at støtte kvinder, men undlader at gøre det, fordi de tror, at deres mangel på personligt interesser i sagen gør deres støtte ud for usandfærdig. 'Der er bevis for, at når en sag virker uforenelig med vores egen interesse, frygter vi at blive mødt med tilbagevirkning, så vi holder os tilbage,' skriver han. Men er denne tavshed bare en undskyldning? Grant siger nej. Forskning understøtter idéen om, at mænd støder på sociale omkostninger, når de fremmer kvinders fremgang — selv når deres hensigter er rene. En undersøgelse fra University of Auckland testede teorien om ambivalente seksisme, som opdeler fordomme mod kvinder i to former: fjendtlig seksisme — åbenlyst fiendtlig adfærd eller overbevisning om kvinders underlegenhed — og velviljende seksisme — den paternale opfattelse, at kvinder har brug for beskyttelse og omsorg. Undersøgelsen fandt, at kvinder med en stærkere fornemmelse af ret til at blive behandlet særligt var mere tilbøjelige til at godkende udsagn som 'Kvinder bør værdsættes og beskyttes af mænd.' Separat forskning af psykologerne Rebecca Ratner (University of Maryland) og Dale Miller (Stanford) viste, at når mænd offentligt støttede kvinders rettigheder, reagerede både mænd og kvinder med overraskelse — ja, endda vrede. I ét eksperiment var deltagere mindre villige til at støtte en fiktiv politik, der gav fordel til det modsatte køn, trods at de viste lige så stor modstand mod politikker, der påvirkede deres eget køn. Grant fortæller et reelt eksempel: da en mand ytrede støtte til øget antal kvinder i ledelse under et workshop, svarede hans kvindelige kolleger ikke med taknemmelighed, men med mistro — og spurgte, om han forsøgte at vinde romantisk fordel. Grant mener, at at fremme kønslig ligestilling kræver mere end at bryde glastagene — det kræver også at nedbryde frygten, der forhindrer mænd i at blive aktive allierede. 'Hemmelige feminister' skal opmuntres til at tale op, ikke stilles til tavshed af tvivl eller social risiko.

article_content: Nine new species of colorful, tree-climbing tarantulas have been discovered in Brazil — including four from the genus Typhochlaena, previously believed extinct. The findings, led by Dr. Rogério Bertani of the Instituto Butantan in São Paulo, increase the number of known tarantula species in the region from seven to sixteen. These arboreal tarantulas exhibit adaptations for life in the canopy: slender bodies, elongated legs, and enhanced surface area on their feet, enabling superior grip and agility on vertical surfaces. Among the discoveries is Typhochlaena amma, found in the mountainous Atlantic Rainforest of Espírito Santo, and Typhochlaena costae, known from the Cerrado savanna. Four new species belong to Typhochlaena — a genus represented by only one known specimen since 1841. Now recognized as the world’s smallest arboreal tarantulas, they are likely evolutionary relics of a once-wider distribution. Two additional new species, Pachistopelma bromelicola and Iridopelma katiae, have been identified living exclusively within bromeliads — water-holding plants that provide shelter from intense sunlight in treeless habitats such as tabletop mountains. Until now, only one species was known to specialize in bromeliads; the discovery of two adds significant ecological insight. These species are highly endemic, confined to small, rapidly degrading habitats under intense pressure from deforestation and land conversion. Their vibrant coloration, while scientifically fascinating, poses a new threat: increased risk of capture for the exotic pet trade. The research, published in the open-access journal ZooKeys, underscores how little is still known about biodiversity in even the most studied ecosystems — especially those under severe human threat.

article_content: Summer Hansen, a 31-year-old special education teacher at Centennial High School in Corona, California, appeared in court on September 12, 2013, to enter a not guilty plea on multiple charges related to alleged sexual misconduct with five underage males. None of the boys were her official students, but all attended the same school. Hansen, a married mother of three, is accused of engaging in sexual activity with the boys in locations including her classroom, a school utility closet, her car, and one student’s home. She is also alleged to have sent them explicit photographs. The prosecution has not yet disclosed whether these images will be presented as evidence. Her defense attorney, David Cohn, argued that the boys — who know each other — are coordinating their stories and may be mistaken or influenced. 'Do teenagers lie? Sure they do. Do they say something and then really believe it and move forward? Yes,' Cohn told local station KTLA. Hansen, who was arrested in June 2013, has since dyed her hair from platinum blonde to light brown. She appeared in court accompanied by a male companion. She has been suspended without pay and is currently under a court order prohibiting contact with minors, except her own children. 'We don’t have any objection to the teaching part of it, but there are family friends, relatives, things of that nature,' Cohn clarified. The investigation began after a school district employee reported concerns about inappropriate relationships. Hansen faces charges of unlawful sexual intercourse and oral copulation with a minor. If convicted, she could receive up to 13 years in prison.

article_content: David Lowe, a BBC radio presenter with over three decades of service, was dismissed after playing a vintage 1932 recording of 'The Sun Has Got His Hat On' during his Sunday night show on Radio Devon. The song, performed by Ambrose & His Orchestra, contains a racially offensive lyric from its era — a word Lowe claims he never heard or recognized. He had planned to issue a sincere apology to listeners on his next broadcast, but BBC management reportedly stopped him, instead urging him to resign. The decision triggered widespread criticism from senior political figures. Former Prime Minister David Cameron called the outcome 'a bit odd,' suggesting the punishment didn’t match the context, especially since only one listener complained and Lowe had no malicious intent. London Mayor Boris Johnson went further, calling the BBC’s actions 'utterly disgraceful' and comparing today’s climate of online outrage to the extremism of groups like Boko Haram — arguing that fear of social media backlash is paralyzing institutions. Critics noted the contrast with Jeremy Clarkson’s case, where a leaked clip allegedly containing the same slur resulted in no termination. Though the BBC later offered Lowe his job back, he declined, citing severe stress that worsened an existing medical condition. The corporation acknowledged it mishandled communications and said the door remains open if he changes his mind.

article_content: Bath have confirmed the signing of Welsh fly-half Rhys Priestland, who will join the club at the end of this season in a bid to challenge England’s George Ford for the No 10 jersey. The 27-year-old, who has earned 32 caps for Wales and made 147 appearances for the Scarlets, is relocating to The Rec on a reported salary of £250,000–£300,000. Despite being sidelined in the Welsh national team by Dan Biggar and with rising contender Gareth Anscombe emerging, Priestland has chosen Bath for the competitive environment and fresh challenge—not as a fallback option. His move comes amid the Welsh Rugby Union’s upcoming dual-contract system, which may restrict his eligibility for future international selection. Yet, Priestland remains hopeful of featuring in Warren Gatland’s plans post-World Cup. Bath’s coaching staff, including head coach Mike Ford and assistant Toby Booth, have been unequivocal: Priestland is not being brought in as cover—he is here to start. Booth emphasized, 'He is coming here to push George and compete for that position.' Priestland’s departure from the Scarlets marks the end of a storied decade-long tenure. Head coach Wayne Pivac praised his leadership, experience, and loyalty, calling him 'a big part of the region' and noting he will 'always be a Scarlet.' Though he has faced harsh criticism from fans, Priestland described his time with the Scarlets as filled with 'great highs and some heartfelt lows.' His decision reflects resilience and ambition, not defeat.

article_content: Jose Mourinho is facing a tough decision: keeping both Thibaut Courtois and Petr Cech at Chelsea this season means one of them will have to sit out — and he knows it will hurt. Still, he sees it as a luxury problem. Cech, who’s returned from a serious shoulder injury, delivered a solid performance in a pre-season match against RZ Pellets WAC after Jeremie Boga equalized Silvio De Oliveira’s opening goal. But despite Cech’s decade-long loyalty and resilience, Courtois — who’s yet to report for training — is the clear favorite to start Chelsea’s Premier League opener against Burnley on August 18. Last season, Courtois helped Atletico Madrid win La Liga and reach the Champions League final, then shone again at the World Cup. Mourinho doesn’t hide his admiration for both: calling Cech one of the top experienced keepers in the world and Courtois the best young keeper alive. He insists the choice isn’t personal — it’s about who gives the team the best chance to win. ‘Chelsea fans won’t care which one plays,’ he says. ‘They’ll be happy knowing we’ve got two of the best in the world between the posts.’ Cech’s recovery was tested in the friendly — stretching his shoulder on crosses, punching under pressure, reacting to low shots — and Mourinho confirmed he’s fully fit. Ultimately, the manager sees this not as a rivalry, but as a rare advantage: two world-class options, and the responsibility to pick the right one at the right time.

Men han ser det som et luxusproblem. Cech, der er tilbage efter en alvorlig skulderskade, ydede en solid præstation i en præ-sæsonkamp mod RZ Pellets WAC, efter at Jeremie Boga ligejorde Silvio De Oliveira's åbningsslag. Men trods Cechs tiårs lange loyaltet og modstandskraft, er Courtois — der endnu ikke har rapporteret til træning — den tydelige favorit til at starte i Chelseas Premier League-åbning mod Burnley den 18. august. Sidste sæson hjalp Courtois Atletico Madrid med at vinde La Liga og nå til Champions League-finalen, og så skinnede han igen ved VM. Mourinho skjuler ikke sin beundring for begge: han kalder Cech en af de øverste erfarne målmænd i verden og Courtois den bedste unge målmand i verden. Han insisterer på, at valget ikke er personligt — det handler om, hvem der giver holdet den bedste chance for at vinde. 'Chelsea-fans vil ikke være ligeglad med, hvem der spiller,' siger han. 'De vil være glade for at vide, at vi har to af de bedste i verden mellem stængerne.' Cechs genopretningsproces blev testet i kampen — han strakte sin skulder på kors, slog under pres og reagerede på lavt skud — og Mourinho bekræftede, at han er fuldt helbredt. I sidste ende ser træneren dette ikke som en rivalisering, men som en sjælden fordel: to verdensklassevalg, og ansvaret for at vælge det rigtige ud fra det rigtige tidspunkt.

article_content: James Rodríguez has cemented his status as one of the standout stars of the 2014 World Cup after being named the tournament’s best goal scorer — not for total goals, but for the single most breathtaking strike. His stunning volley against Uruguay in the Round of 16, a perfectly timed chest control followed by a swivel and thunderous strike that clipped the crossbar and left goalkeeper Fernando Muslera rooted, earned him over 4 million votes from FIFA.com users. The goal, which opened the scoring in Colombia’s 2-0 win at Rio’s iconic Maracanã Stadium, was widely regarded as a masterpiece of technique and composure. Runner-up in the public vote was Netherlands captain Robin van Persie, whose acrobatic header against Spain in a 5-1 win remains one of the most memorable moments of the tournament. But Rodríguez’s effort stood apart — not just for its beauty, but for its timing and impact on a global stage. This honor adds to his already historic World Cup campaign: Rodríguez finished as the Golden Boot winner with six goals, leading Colombia to the quarter-finals. He is now poised to join Real Madrid in a reported £60 million transfer from AS Monaco. His achievement continues a South American streak — he follows Uruguay’s Diego Forlán (2010) and Argentina’s Maxi Rodríguez (2006) as the third consecutive winner from the continent. With this award, Rodríguez didn’t just score a goal — he delivered a moment that will be replayed for decades.

article_content: Meet Freddie — the first British baby born thanks to a groundbreaking fertility treatment that uses music. His parents, Isabelle and Stephen from Liverpool, endured two miscarriages and a failed IVF cycle before discovering an experimental technique at Barcelona’s Institut Marquès. There, scientists play music continuously in IVF incubators to see if sound vibrations can boost fertilization rates. Researchers exposed nearly 1,000 eggs to music — including tracks by Michael Jackson, Madonna, Nirvana, Metallica, Bach, Mozart, and Vivaldi — while keeping half in silent incubators as controls. To their surprise, fertilization rates rose by approximately 5% in the music-exposed group. Although embryos cannot hear until at least 14 weeks, scientists believe the subtle vibrations from sound waves help nutrients enter the egg and accelerate the removal of metabolic waste — mimicking the natural rocking motion eggs experience as they travel through the fallopian tube. Pop, heavy metal, and classical music all showed similar effects, suggesting it’s the physical vibration, not genre, that matters. While it’s too early to confirm if this improves live birth rates, couples in 17 countries, including the UK, have already welcomed babies using this method. Now one year old, Freddie shows a clear fascination with music — especially turning the dials of a large radio placed near him during playtime. His parents hope learning about his musical origins will make him feel uniquely special. Dr. Carolina Castello, a researcher at Institut Marquès, notes there’s no harm in couples trying to conceive naturally playing music they enjoy. 'Music is beneficial for everything,' she says — a sentiment echoed by many hopeful parents.

article_content: Last week, Dr. Roberto Feliz and Dr. Hiba Georges left the advanced facilities of Boston Medical Center for a harrowing reality in Port-au-Prince, Haiti — delivering emergency care inside two tents operated by the University of Miami. With no electricity, no lab tests, and barely any tools, they were forced to make life-or-death decisions based on instinct and observation alone. Their first major lesson came when a young boy needed an emergency amputation to survive a crushing injury. Without an operating room available, they waited hours for help that never arrived. In desperation, they performed the procedure under moonlight beneath a mango tree. The boy was unconscious from shock, so no anesthesia was needed — but it was too late. He died mid-surgery. The moment shattered the team. Some wept. Feliz told them, 'There’s no crying in medicine.' But that night, something changed. By 3 a.m., the team began building their own operating room — with no lights, no oxygen, no blood supply. One surgeon used his belt as a tourniquet. A few hours later, another boy, 16, showed signs of kidney failure. Without blood tests, the only indicator was urine. None came. Despite IV fluids and diuretics, the boy passed away. Feliz says that loss cut deeper than any other. He texted his wife: 'I’ve had a bad day.' Afterward, the team became quicker to authorize amputations — knowing delay meant death. What began as a mission of aid became a brutal education in humility. Back in Boston, Feliz was treated like a top specialist. Here, he scrubbed floors, hauled bodies through the streets, and rode in overloaded vehicles carrying the dead. 'I came in thinking I was a hero,' he says. 'I’m leaving as someone who finally understands what real medicine looks like.'
translated_content: Sidste uge forlod lægerne Roberto Feliz og Hiba Georges de avancerede faciliteter ved Boston Medical Center for en skræmmende virkelighed i Port-au-Prince, Haiti — hvor de ydede akut medicinsk hjælp i to telt, der blev drevet af University of Miami. Med ingen strøm, ingen laboratorietests og næsten ingen værktøjer var de tvunget til at træffe livs-eller-døds-afgørelser baseret på intuition og observation. Deres første store lærdom kom, da en ung dreng havde brug for en akut amputation for at overleve et pressehjul. Da der ikke var nogen operationssal til rådighed, ventede de timer på hjælp, der aldrig kom. I desperation udførte de proceduren under måneskin under en mangotræ. Drengen var bevidstløs af chok, så der var ingen behov for anæstesi — men det var for sent. Han døde under operationen. Øjeblikket slog holdet. Nogle græd. Feliz sagde til dem: 'Der er ikke plads til gråd i medicin.' Men den nat skete noget. Kl. 3 om morgenen begyndte holdet at bygge deres egen operationssal — uden lys, ilt eller blod. En kirurg brugte sin belte som tourniquet. Et par timer senere viste en anden dreng, 16 år, tegn på nyresvigt. Uden blodtests var den eneste indikator urin. Ingen kom. Trods intravenøse væsker og diuretika døde drengen. Feliz siger, at dette tab skar dybere end noget andet. Han sendte en tekst til sin hustru: 'Jeg har haft en dårlig dag.' Efterfølgende blev holdet hurtigere til at godkende amputationer — fordi de vidste, at forsinkelse betød død. Det, der startede som en mission om at hjælpe, blev en brutal uddannelse i beskedethed. Tilbage i Boston blev Feliz behandlet som en top-specialist. Her skrubbede han gulve, bar døde kroppe gennem gaderne og kørte i overfyldte køretøjer med de døde. 'Jeg kom her og troede, jeg var en helt,' siger han. 'Jeg forlader som nogen, der endelig forstår, hvad ægte medicin ser ud til.'
post_content: From Boston’s high-tech hospitals to a tent under a mango tree — these doctors did surgery by moonlight with a belt as a tourniquet. No labs. No lights. Just heart. 💔 #HaitiRelief #MedicineWithoutBorders #RealHeroes
translated_post: Fra Bostons moderne sygehuse til et telt under et mangotræ — disse læger udførte operationer under måneskin med en belte som tourniquet. Ingen labtests. Ingen lys. Kun hjerte. 💔 #HaitiHjælp #MedicinUdenGrænser #ÆgteHelte

article_content: Recently, scuba divers off the coast of Costa Rica had an extraordinary encounter with a giant oceanic manta ray — not because they sought it out, but because it seemed to seek them out. The massive fish, weighing up to 5,000 pounds and spanning 18 feet across its wings, was entangled in thick fishing line, its movements restricted and visibly strained. To the divers’ surprise, the manta approached them closely, as if requesting assistance. Without hesitation, the team carefully cut away the entangling cords. Once freed, the ray executed a powerful, energetic flip before swimming off into the open ocean — a moment captured on video by one of the divers. In a touching gesture, the divers kept a small piece of the discarded fishing line as a memento. 'We picked up the line. It’s our trophy now,' said Brian, the diver who severed the cords, adding that he shared fragments with everyone present. The giant oceanic manta ray (Mobula birostris) is the largest species of ray and belongs to the eagle ray family. Scientists consider it to have the largest brain of any fish species, though its full cognitive capacity remains unproven. Like whale sharks and baleen whales, mantas are filter feeders, consuming only microscopic plankton and small organisms. They are known for long-distance migrations, often crossing entire ocean basins. This rare interaction highlights both the vulnerability of these gentle giants to marine debris and the profound impact humans can have when they intervene compassionately.
translated_content: For nylig havde dykkere ved kysten af Costa Rica et ekstraordinært møde med en gigantisk oceanisk manta-ray — ikke fordi de søgte den, men fordi den synes at have søgt dem. Den massive fisk, der vejer op til 2.268 kg og har et vingeudspænd på 5,5 meter, var fanget i tykt fiskeri snor, med bevægelser, der var begrænset og tydeligt belastet. Til dykkernes overraskelse nærmede manta-ray sig dem tæt, som om den bad om hjælp. Uden at tøve skar holdet forsigtigt løs de fangne snore. Når den var fri, udførte ray’en en kraftig, energisk vandring før den svømmede ud i det åbne ocean — et øjeblik fanget på video af en af dykkerne. I en rørende gestus beholdt dykkerne et lille stykke af den kasserede snor som et minde. 'Vi tog snoren op. Den er vores trophy nu!' sagde Brian, dykkeren, der skar snoren løs, og tilføjede, at han delte stykker med alle til stede. Den gigantiske oceaniske manta-ray (Mobula birostris) er den største ray-art og tilhører ædle ray-familien. Videnskabsmænd anses for at have den største hjerne af enhver fisk, selvom dens fulde kognitive kapacitet er uafklaret. Ligesom hvalhajer og baleinhvaler er mantarayer filtrerende fødere, der kun spiser mikroskopiske plankton og små organismer. De er kendt for lange distancer migrationer og ofte krydser hele oceanner. Denne sjældne interaktion understreger både sårbarheden af disse blide giganter over for marint affald og den dybe indvirkning mennesker kan have, når de intervenere med medfølelse.

article_content: Walmart has announced it is re-editing a commercial featuring a Black man mouthing 'I can't breathe,' after viewers expressed concern that it evoked the death of Eric Garner. The ad, promoting Walmart Family Mobile, shows a father handing a cellphone to his overjoyed daughter, who hugs him tightly. As he struggles playfully to breathe under her embrace, he mouths, 'I can't breathe,' clearly in jest. The commercial first aired over the summer but gained renewed attention following the high-profile death of Eric Garner, a 43-year-old father who died in July after being placed in a chokehold by NYPD officer Daniel Pantaleo. In video footage, Garner repeatedly cried out, 'I can't breathe, I can't breathe' as he was restrained. In the aftermath of the grand jury’s decision not to indict Pantaleo, the phrase 'I can't breathe' became a nationwide rallying cry for protesters demanding justice. Many viewers took to Twitter to express discomfort, with one commenting: '#Walmart, did you really just air a commercial in New York showing a young Black girl hugging her dad while he says #ICantBreathe?' Walmart responded quickly, acknowledging the ad’s timing was unfortunate and stating, 'We can see how the ad could be viewed differently today than when it first aired. We're re-editing.' Some observers noted that while the ad itself was harmless, the timing was deeply insensitive given recent events. Others defended the company, pointing out that no corporation could have predicted the resurgence of the phrase in protest contexts.
translated_content: Walmart har meddelt, at det reviderer en reklame, der viser en sort mand, der mumler 'I can't breathe', efter at seere udtrykte bekymring for, at den mindede om Eric Garners død. Reklamen, der fremhæver Walmart Family Mobile, viser en far, der giver sin overglade datter en mobiltelefon, som kaster sig om hans hals og trykker ham tæt til sig. Mens han latterligt kæmper for luft under hendes omfavnelse, mumler han: 'I can't breathe', tydeligt i latterlig tone. Reklamen blev vist første gang i sommeren, men fik ny opmærksomhed efter Eric Garners højt profilerede død i juli, da den 43-årige far døde efter at være blevet lagt i en chokhold af NYPD-officer Daniel Pantaleo. I videomateriale kan Garner høres sige gentagne gange: 'I can't breathe, I can't breathe', mens han blev nedsat. Efter den store jury's beslutning om ikke at anklage Pantaleo, blev sætningen 'I can't breathe' et landdækkende kampord for demonstranter, der krævede retfærdighed. Mange seere tog til Twitter for at udtrykke udfordring, hvor en kommentator skrev: '#Walmart, har I virkelig lige sendt en reklame i New York, hvor en ung sort pige har armene omkring sin fars hals, mens han siger #ICantBreathe?' Walmart svarede hurtigt og erkendte, at tidspunktet var uheldigt: 'Vi kan se, hvordan reklamen kan opfattes anderledes i dag end da den først blev vist. Vi reviderer den.' Nogle observatører bemærkede, at reklamen selv var ufarlig, men at tidspunktet var dybt følsomt givet de seneste begivenheder. Andre forsvarer virksomheden og peger på, at ingen virksomhed kunne forudsige genopstået brug af sætningen i protester.

article_content: Imagine receiving an email from your spouse suggesting you apply for a one-way trip to Mars. Would you be horrified — or inspired? That’s exactly what happened to Dr. Leila Zucker, a 46-year-old emergency doctor in Washington, when her husband sent her details about Mars One last spring. He told her he didn’t want her to go… but felt he’d be failing as a partner if he didn’t tell her about it. Today, Zucker is among just 705 people chosen from over 200,000 applicants to move forward in the selection process. The goal? To send the first four humans to Mars in 2024 — permanently. There’s no return planned. Technological hurdles, funding gaps, and the sheer impossibility of sustaining life on Mars haven’t deterred these pioneers. Mars One, led by CEO Bas Lansdorp, plans to finance the mission largely through a global reality TV spectacle, betting that audiences will pay to watch humans live and die on another planet. Critics say the tech isn’t ready — no one has ever landed on Mars with life support, and no system has been tested in Martian conditions. But Mars One insists it’s all based on existing, proven hardware. Meanwhile, candidates are preparing: simulation habitats are being built to mimic Martian life. For Zucker, the hardest part isn’t the radiation or the dust storms — it’s saying goodbye to her husband of 21 years. She says she’ll likely offer him a divorce, but still wear her wedding ring. He supports her dream, even though he fears losing her. Others face similar heartbreak. Dan Carey, 52, worries his wife will have to watch him die on live TV. Sachin Desai and his wife, Ankita, applied as a team — they believe their bond is strong enough to survive a lifetime on Mars. For Harvard grad student Marina Santiago, the mission is less about the planet and more about human connection: on Mars, your crewmates become your family. Even religious leaders have weighed in — the UAE’s Islamic authority issued a fatwa warning Muslims against joining, citing the near-certainty of death. Mars One responded respectfully, inviting dialogue. Some applicants, like Gregory Sachs, hope future missions will bring people home. Others, like Brian Robles, shrug: ‘We’re all going to die someday. Why not make it count?’ And then there’s the food: Carey plans to lose weight just to fit more chocolate in his suitcase. Zucker dreams of growing beef from lab-grown stem cells. Michael McDonnell wants to bake the first pizza on Mars. It’s not just science — it’s a deeply human story of love, loss, courage, and the wild, beautiful urge to reach beyond the horizon.

article_content: According to reports in Spain, Real Madrid defender Raphaël Varane is eager to discuss his future with manager Carlo Ancelotti following the World Cup. Marca claims the French international is frustrated with his limited role as a backup to Sergio Ramos and Pepe, and may consider leaving the Santiago Bernabéu this summer. Varane started only 12 league games last season due to a knee injury, but he played the full 120 minutes in Real Madrid’s extra-time victory over Atlético Madrid in the 2014 UEFA Champions League final. The 21-year-old was a key figure for France at the 2014 World Cup in Brazil, starting four of their five matches as they reached the quarter-finals. At club level, Ancelotti has consistently favored the experienced pairing of Ramos and Pepe in central defense, limiting Varane’s opportunities. Marca reports that Ancelotti intends to assure Varane that he remains a vital part of Real Madrid’s long-term plans to prevent him from joining a Premier League club. Chelsea manager José Mourinho, who has long admired the defender, is among those monitoring his situation. Mourinho was Chelsea’s manager when Varane moved to Real Madrid in 2011, but did not sign him. Other top-flight English clubs are also keeping tabs on Varane’s status. However, Real Madrid teammate Karim Benzema is expected to encourage him to remain in the Spanish capital.

Marca påstår, at den franske international er utilfreds med sin begrænsede rolle som reservebag Sergio Ramos og Pepe, og kan overveje at forlade Santiago Bernabéu denne sommer. Varane startede kun 12 liga-kampe sidste sæson på grund af en knæskade, men han spillede de fulde 120 minutter i Real Madrids ekstra-tids-sejr mod Atlético Madrid i finalen i UEFA Champions League 2014. Den 21-årige var en nøglefigur for Frankrig ved VM 2014 i Brasilien, hvor han startede fire af deres fem kampe, mens holdet nåede kvartfinalen. På klubniveau har Ancelotti konsekvent foretrukket den erfarnede duo Ramos og Pepe i midterforsvaret, hvilket har begrænset Varanes muligheder. Marca rapporterer, at Ancelotti vil forsikre Varane om, at han stadig er en vigtig del af Real Madrids langsigtede planer for at forhindre ham i at skifte til en Premier League-klub. Chelsea-træner José Mourinho, der længe har været en beundrer af forsvareren, følger hans situation. Mourinho var Chelsea-træner, da Varane gik til Real Madrid i 2011, men han signerede ham ikke. Andre topklubber i England holder også øje med Varanes situation. Dog forventes det, at Real Madrid-kammerat Karim Benzema vil opfordre ham til at blive i den spanske hovedstad.

article_content: AP McCoy has matched the legendary career win total of retired trainer Martin Pipe, both now sitting on 4,191 victories after McCoy rode On The Record to triumph at Uttoxeter. The moment was deeply personal for McCoy, who shares a long-standing friendship and good-natured rivalry with Pipe. 'He’s an inspiration to every jockey and everyone involved in racing,' Pipe said, praising McCoy’s enduring impact on the sport. McCoy, known for his quiet determination, remarked with a smile that the horse’s name — On The Record — felt almost too perfect. The two have exchanged plenty of banter over the years about who might eventually hold the record, and Pipe has even joked he might reapply for his trainer’s license if McCoy pulls ahead. David Pipe, who now runs the family stable in Somerset, captured the spirit of the occasion on Twitter: 'Could there be a more fitting way for @AP_McCoy to join my dad in the 4191 club than winning on On The Record? #McCoyWatch.' With five more rides scheduled for Thursday, McCoy has a real shot at making history — and possibly driving his old friend a little crazy in the process.

Øjeblikket var dybt personligt for McCoy, der har en langvarig venlighed og en venlig rivalisering med Pipe. 'Han er en inspiration for alle jockeys og alle i ræsverdenen,' sagde Pipe og lovpriste McCoeys vedvarende indflydelse på sporten. McCoy, kendt for sin stille bestemmethed, bemærkede med et smil, at hestens navn — On The Record — føltes næsten for perfekt. De to har gennem årene udvekslet mange latterlige kommentarer om, hvem der endelig vil holde rekorden, og Pipe har endda jokeret om, at han måske vil ansøge om sin trænerlicens igen, hvis McCoy trækker forbi. David Pipe, der nu leder familiens stab i Somerset, fangede ånden i øjeblikket på Twitter: 'Kunne der være en mere passende måde for @AP_McCoy at blive medlem af min fars 4191-klub end at vinde med On The Record? #McCoyWatch.' Med fem flere rytterier planlagt torsdag har McCoy en reel chance for at skrive historie — og muligvis drive sin gamle ven lidt gal.

article_content: Many Berkshire Hathaway Inc. investors may have cherished Charlie Munger’s quips almost as much as the staggering 3.8 million percent return he helped generate. Munger, who passed away in California just under a month before his 100th birthday, was Warren Buffett’s longtime business partner. Together, they transformed Berkshire from a struggling textile mill into a $783 billion industrial giant spanning insurance, energy, and beyond. Each year, the duo captivated audiences at Berkshire’s shareholder meeting in Omaha, Nebraska. Munger also drew devoted crowds annually to Daily Journal Corp’s gatherings in Los Angeles. His direct, incisive style stood in sharp contrast to Buffett’s warm, folksy demeanor — a dynamic that made their appearances legendary. Industry leaders like Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan and former Wells Fargo CEO Tim Sloan hailed Munger as 'legendary.' Sloan added that Munger was 'a generous philanthropist whose unfiltered advice and refreshing perspectives positively impacted businesses around the world.' Munger was renowned for his unforgettable one-liners. To his devoted followers — whom he affectionately called 'groupies' — he shared hard-won life lessons. In 2015, he warned that future generations would struggle to maintain their standard of living: 'Somebody my age has lived through the best and easiest period that ever happened in the history of the world — the lowest death rates, the highest investment productivity, biggest increases in most people’s standards of living. If you’re unhappy with what you’ve had over the last 50 years, you have an unfortunate misapprehension of life.' He frequently condemned financial recklessness. In 2011, he blamed the pre-crisis U.S. bubble on 'megalomania, insanity, and evil,' and sharply criticized former Fed Chair Alan Greenspan: 'Alan Greenspan is a smart man. He just totally overdosed on Ayn Rand at a young age.' He later mocked Greeks for believing they could vote themselves wealthy amid debt crises, and dismissed derivatives trading desks as 'a casino in drag' — adding, 'They make the witch doctors look good.' Munger was a vocal critic of cryptocurrency, calling Bitcoin 'noxious poison' and digital assets 'partly fraud and partly delusion.' In a 2022 CNBC interview, he stated: 'That’s a bad combination. I don’t like either fraud or delusion. And the delusion may be more extreme than the fraud.' Though supportive of Republican causes, Munger never hesitated to criticize his own side. In 2017, he warned Republican leaders against dismantling financial oversight: 'My fellow Republicans — the ones taking away all this regulation of major finance — I think that’s bonkers.' He also criticized Bernie Sanders, calling him 'an intellectual disgrace' — though he added, 'I don’t think he’s any worse than some of our Republicans. But at least they’re crazy in a different way.' Above all, Munger and Buffett’s brilliance lay in their ability to distill complexity into clarity. For Berkshire’s 50th anniversary, Munger wrote a five-page letter explaining the company’s success: 'In its early Buffett years, Berkshire had a big task ahead: turning a tiny stash into a large and useful company. And it solved that problem by avoiding bureaucracy and relying much on one thoughtful leader for a long, long time as he kept improving and brought in more people like himself. Compare this to a typical big-corporation system with much bureaucracy at headquarters and a long succession of CEOs who come in at about age 59, pause little thereafter for quiet thought, and are soon forced out by a fixed retirement age.'

Senere satte han grin med grækerne for at tro, de kunne stemme sig selv til rigdom under gældskriser, og afviste derivathandel som 'et kasino i drag' – og tilføjede: 'De gør troldmændene til at se godt ud.' Munger var en vokal kritiker af kryptowægt, og kaldte Bitcoin 'giftig gift' og digitale aktiver 'delvis svindel og delvis illusion.' I et interview med CNBC i 2022 sagde han: 'Det er en dårlig kombination. Jeg kan ikke lide hverken svindel eller illusion. Og illusionen kan være mere ekstrem end svindelen.' Selv om han støttede republikanske årsager, undgik Munger aldrig at kritisere sit eget parti. I 2017 advarede han republikanske ledere mod at fjerne finansiel tilsyn: 'Mine medrepublikanere – dem, der fjerner alt dette tilsyn af store finansier – jeg synes det er bonkers.' Han kritiserede også Bernie Sanders og kaldte ham 'en intellektuel skam' – men tilføjede: 'Jeg tror ikke, han er værre end nogle af vores republikanere. Men i det mindste er de gale på en anden måde.' Først og fremmest lå Munger og Buffetts genialitet i deres evne til at formilde kompleksitet med klarsyn. Til Berkshire’s 50-års jubilæum skrev Munger et fem-siders brev, der forklarede virksomhedens succes: 'I sine tidlige Buffett-år havde Berkshire en stor opgave foran sig: at omdanne en lille beholdning til et stort og nyttigt selskab. Og det løste problemet ved at undgå bureaukrati og stort set stole på én tænkende leder i lang, lang tid, mens han forbedrede sig og tog flere mennesker som sig selv med. Sammenlign dette med et typisk stort virksomhedssystem med meget bureaukrati i hovedkvarteret og en lang række CEO’er, der kommer ind ved cirka 59 år, næsten aldrig pauser til stille tanke, og snart bliver tvunget ud af en fast pensionsalder.'

article_content: As the Premier League kicks off this weekend, Sportsmail breaks down everything you need to know ahead of West Ham’s home opener against Tottenham at Upton Park — Saturday at 3pm. With referee Chris Foy in charge, fans can expect a fiery London derby filled with history and fresh narratives. For West Ham, boss Sam Allardyce faces a tough start: long-term injury victim Andy Carroll is out, and summer signing Enner Valencia isn’t quite match-fit yet. Newcomer Diafra Sakho, who only joined on Thursday, might make his debut if he passes fitness tests. Matt Jarvis is sidelined with a thigh issue, while Ravel Morrison and Carl Jenkinson are doubtful due to groin and hamstring problems respectively. On the Spurs side, manager Mauricio Pochettino is waiting to assess several players returning from World Cup duty — including Jan Vertonghen, Mousa Dembele, Nacer Chadli, and Paulinho. Good news: Andros Townsend has shaken off his ankle knock and looks set to feature. New signings Michel Vorm, Ben Davies, and Eric Dier are all fit and ready to go. Kyle Walker, Michael Dawson, and Vlad Chiriches remain under evaluation for pelvic, ankle, and back issues. Statistically, last season was challenging for Tottenham — West Ham beat them twice in the league and once in the Capital One Cup. Meanwhile, West Ham had the worst shooting accuracy in the 2013–14 campaign, converting only 37% of their efforts on target — though Valencia, now at West Ham, hit 3 goals from just 5 shots on target during the World Cup. This clash also marks Allardyce’s 400th Premier League game as a manager. It’s a rematch of the 1999/2000 season opener, when Harry Redknapp’s West Ham edged Tottenham 1-0 at Upton Park. article_content: Matthew Sanchez had rarely seen his father cry — until the day he watched the X-rays of his own spine. After a devastating high school football injury in 2004, 15-year-old Matthew suffered a fractured C5 vertebra. His father, Rudjard Hayes, held his wife close, overcome with emotion, unaware that Matthew could see him. Doctors said recovery was nearly impossible. But Matthew was determined. At Shepherd Center in Atlanta, surgeons inserted a plate, screws, cables, and a bone graft from his leg. Within days, Matthew began moving. Five weeks later, he walked out of the center. Six months after that, his life felt normal again. Two years later, he was competing as an athlete once more. His survival was due in large part to Dr. John Henderson, the opposing team’s doctor, who held Matthew’s head steady for 45 minutes in the mud — refusing to let anyone move him — and insisted on a helicopter transport. His mother believes this prevented permanent paralysis. A year later, the family learned that Dr. Henderson’s son, Army Ranger John Henderson Jr., had been killed in Afghanistan. 'He saved our son,' Lorraine Hayes said, 'and lost his own.' Now 20, Matthew didn’t take a summer break. Instead, he rode 4,350 miles across the U.S. with three friends to raise money for Shepherd Center’s SHARE program — a partnership that provides elite care and housing for veterans with spinal injuries, brain trauma, and chronic pain. The ride honored John Henderson Jr. and supported soldiers like Spc. Dillon Cannon, who survived a sniper attack in Iraq. ‘They risk their lives every day,’ Matthew said. ‘They deserve the best.’ His journey wasn’t just about recovery — it was about paying it forward.

Hans far, Rudjard Hayes, holdt sin kone tæt til sig, overvældet af følelser, uden at vide, at Matthew kunne se ham. Lægerne sagde, at genoprejsning var næsten umulig. Men Matthew var bestemt. article_content: Water companies were ordered yesterday to slash bills — but households will still end up paying more due to inflation. Regulator Ofwat instructed suppliers to reduce average customer bills by 5% by 2020, cutting them from £396 to £376. As part of a new five-year plan, companies must invest £44 billion to reduce water leaks by 370 million litres per day and minimize the duration of water outages caused by repairs. Although bills are being cut by 5%, customers will pay more in real terms because companies can raise annual bills in line with RPI (Retail Price Index) inflation — currently 2.3%. Many households will see bills exceed £400 for the first time next year. By 2020, assuming the same inflation rate, bills could reach £420. This will hit older customers on fixed incomes especially hard, as state benefits and many occupational pensions rise only in line with CPI (Consumer Price Index), which stands at just 1.3%. To support the most vulnerable, Ofwat requires companies to extend social tariffs to an additional one million households. These offer discounts of up to 25% off standard bills. A key reason Ofwat pushed for lower bills is the reduced cost of borrowing for infrastructure projects. Cathryn Ross, Ofwat’s chief executive, said: 'With bills held down by 5% and service improved over the next five years, customers will get more and pay less.' Jonson Cox, Ofwat chairman, added: 'We are bringing down bills so customers can expect value for money, while investors earn a fair return. Companies will need to do more with the same level of funding as before.' Northumbrian customers will see the smallest reduction — a 1% cut to £382. Tony Smith, CEO of the Consumer Council for Water, welcomed the bill reductions without service cuts, calling it 'the best process for customers since privatisation.' However, he cautioned that inflation-linked pricing may still leave many worse off. He also noted: 'Ofwat has been generous to the sector in previous reviews.'

Mange husholdninger vil se deres regninger overstige £400 for første gang næste år. Inden 2020, under antagelse af samme inflationsrate, kunne regningerne nå £420. article_content: Kevin Nolan insists he did not hear any boos from West Ham supporters when he came on as a substitute during their 2-0 home victory over QPR before the international break. Though some sections of the crowd appeared to express disapproval at his introduction, Nolan told the Evening Standard that he himself heard nothing. His father and brother, who were in the stands, reported hearing boos—but Nolan attributes this to a small minority. The West Ham captain, known for his industrious midfield play and 17 goals in 56 Premier League appearances for the club, emphasized that his role upon entering the game was to organize play under manager Sam Allardyce’s instructions. 'If people want to boo, that’s up to them,' he said. 'I don’t read websites, but I’ve been told many fans were upset by the reaction—and I appreciate that.' Nolan highlighted his respected legacy at previous clubs, noting that Bolton and Newcastle supporters still regard him fondly. 'I’m part of a fantastic squad. I’m trying to do my best, and I always will. I’ll know when it’s time to go—or the gaffer or chairman will. Until then, I give 100%.' He dismissed the boos as unwarranted: 'They won’t get a reaction out of me—though maybe out of my dad, because he wasn’t happy. To me, it was nothing, because I know it wasn’t deserved. The negative voices always shout louder than the majority who are there to support the team.' West Ham, sitting seventh in the Premier League with 10 points from seven matches, travel to face winless Burnley on Saturday.

Hans far og bror, som var i tribunen, rapporterede, at de hørte buer — men Nolan tilskriver dette en mindrehed. Nolan fremhævede sit respekterede arv hos tidligere klubber og bemærkede, at Bolton- og Newcastle-fans stadig ser på ham med venlighed. 'Jeg er en del af et fantastisk hold. Jeg prøver at gøre mit bedste, og jeg vil altid gøre det. Jeg vil vide, når det er tid til at gå — eller træneren eller direktøren vil. Indtil da, giver jeg 100 %.' Han afviste buerne som uretfærdige: 'De får ingen reaktion ud af mig — selvom måske ud af min far, fordi han ikke var glad. For mig var det ingenting, for jeg ved, det ikke var fortjent. De negative stemmer skriger altid højere end majoriteten, der er der for at støtte holdet.' West Ham står på syvende plads i Premier League med 10 point fra syv kampe og rejser til at møde tabefri Burnley på lørdag.

article_content: In Las Vegas, a 13-year-old girl named Selena sits in a bright orange jail jumpsuit, her wrists and ankles chained, preparing to face a judge—not as a criminal, but as someone who was sold for sex. She dreams of returning to her suburban home, to her baby sister, and to a life that feels normal again. But the court has decided she can’t go home—not because she did anything wrong, but because no one believes she’ll stay safe. Selena, tearfully pleading, says, 'All I want is to be with my family.' She was picked up by undercover officers on the Strip after being exploited by a pimp who met her online via Backpage.com. He gave her drugs, took every dollar she made, and made her see four or five clients daily. 'It made me feel disgusting,' she recalls. 'I just wanted to shower forever.' Despite being a victim under the law, authorities fear she’ll run again, drawn back by the false affection of a predator who once told her, 'Do you need a ride?'—and who she 'was straight up obsessed' with. Her mother, a schoolteacher, shows us Selena’s room: posters, stuffed animals, and lipstick scribbles on the mirror—names of boys she doesn’t recognize. 'I don’t know what’s happening,' she admits. 'She doesn’t tell me anything.' This isn’t an isolated case. According to the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children, between 100,000 and 300,000 American children are trafficked each year, mostly online. After Craigslist removed its adult services section in 2010, traffickers moved en masse to Backpage.com, which reportedly earned $20 million that year. CNN tested the site using a photo of a 14-year-old reporter; dozens of men responded, some offering tens of thousands of dollars for sex. Backpage denies wrongdoing and claims to have improved safety measures—but refuses to speak publicly. Now, Selena is being sent to a treatment center in Utah to address her drug use. A nonprofit stands ready to help her long-term. But no one can promise she’ll ever find her way back to the girl she was at 11—happy, in school, just wanting to watch TV after homework. Her mother says softly, 'I just wish she could be normal, even for one day.'

Hun drømmer om at vende tilbage til sit forstadshus, til sin yngre søster, og til et liv, der føles normalt igen. Men retten har besluttet, at hun ikke kan gå hjem — ikke fordi hun har gjort noget galt, men fordi ingen tror, at hun vil blive tryg. Selena, tårer i øjnene, siger: 'Alt, jeg vil, er at være med min familie.' Hun blev fanget af incognito politifolk på Strippen efter at være udnyttet af en pædofile, der mødte hende online via Backpage.com. Han gav hende narkotika, tog hver eneste dollar, hun tjente, og tvang hende til at se fire eller fem kunder dagligt. 'Det gjorde mig grim,' husker hun. 'Jeg ville bare have taget en dusj for evigt.' Trods at hun er en ofre ifølge loven, frygter myndighederne, at hun vil løbe væk igen, trukket tilbage af en fornærmelse, der engang sagde: 'Har du brug for en tur?' — og som hun 'var helt besat af'. Hendes mor, en lærer, viser os Selenas værelse: plakater, dukker og læppelipstift-skrevne navne på spejlet — navne, hun ikke kender. 'Jeg ved ikke, hvad der sker,' indrømmer hun. 'Hun fortæller mig ikke noget.' Dette er ikke en isoleret sag. Ifølge National Center for Missing and Exploited Children er mellem 100.000 og 300.000 amerikanske børn handler hvert år, primært online. Efter at Craigslist fjernede sin voksen-tjenestesektion i 2010, flyttede menneskehandlere i massevis til Backpage.com, som ifølge rapporter tjente 20 millioner dollar det år. CNN testede websitet med et foto af en 14-årig journalist; dobbelt så mange mænd svarede, nogle tilbød titusinder af dollars for seks. Backpage nægter udtalelse og påstår, at de har forbedret sikkerhedsforanstaltninger — men nægter at tale offentligt. Nu bliver Selena sendt til et behandlingscenter i Utah for at behandle hendes narkotikaproblemer. En stiftelse står klar til at hjælpe hende på lang sigt. Men ingen kan love, at hun nogensinde vil finde vejen tilbage til den pige, hun var ved 11 — lykkelig, i skole, bare ønskede at se TV efter lektier. Hendes mor siger blidt: 'Jeg ønsker bare, at hun kunne være almindelig, selv kun for en dag.'

article_content: In a dramatic escalation of the Occupy movement, protesters in Oakland successfully halted operations at one of the nation’s most critical shipping hubs — the Port of Oakland — after a five-hour standoff that turned violent. What began as a largely peaceful daytime demonstration involving thousands evolved into nighttime chaos, with some demonstrators smashing bank windows, setting fires to dumpsters, and breaching a vacant building. Police responded with tear gas, flashbang grenades, and mass arrests, claiming the violence stemmed from a small group of anarchists. Yet organizers like Boots Riley hailed the event as a historic win, arguing that disrupting the flow of goods was a powerful way to spotlight economic injustice — a message they say mainstream media had ignored until now. The port, which handles billions in trade annually — including electronics, cars from Toyota and Honda, and agricultural exports — was forced to suspend operations due to safety concerns. Maritime workers, truckers, and their families now face lost wages and economic strain, a consequence protesters acknowledge but argue is necessary to force change. Meanwhile, solidarity protests flared across the country: in Seattle, demonstrators confronted JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon outside a hotel; in Baltimore, activists refused to vacate their encampment despite being cut off from electricity; in Minneapolis, officials banned overnight sleeping when temperatures dropped below freezing and removed portable toilets. New York Mayor Michael Bloomberg urged protesters to respect residential neighborhoods, warning they would be removed if they didn’t. In Philadelphia, activists were arrested during a sit-in at Comcast’s headquarters. Veterans in New York marched in uniform to the Stock Exchange, while students in Boston protested student debt at Bank of America branches. Despite the turmoil, many participants — including single mothers, students, and veterans — insisted their cause was rooted in dignity, not destruction. 'There's absolutely something wrong with the system,' said Jessica Medina, an Oakland café worker and part-time student. 'We need to change that.' While some saw the port shutdown as a strategic triumph, others within the movement condemned the violence, distancing themselves from those who broke windows or ignited fires. Police reported dozens of arrests and widespread property damage to both private and public buildings. Yet the emotional core of the protests remained: a cry against inequality, militarized policing, and a financial system perceived as rigged. As cleanup crews worked the next day in Zuccotti Park and other sites, the movement’s future hung in the balance — not as a unified organization, but as a scattered, passionate chorus demanding accountability.

article_content: Last Thursday, employees at a Jack in the Box in Fort Worth, Texas, panicked and locked themselves inside a freezer after a group of armed men entered the restaurant. Fearing a robbery, they fled the service counter — but the men were not criminals. They were members of Open Carry Texas, a pro-gun advocacy group conducting a legal open-carry demonstration. Police responded swiftly, deploying an estimated 10 squad cars and more than 15 officers, all believing they were confronting a violent armed robbery. 'I would estimate around 10 squad cars showed up, some with two per squad car,' said demonstrator Edwin Haros to NBC 5. Sgt. Ray Bush of the Fort Worth Police Department explained that staff acted out of fear: 'They locked themselves inside a freezer for protection, believing the rifle-carrying men would rob them.' He added that the group displayed no signage and did not notify police beforehand — making their intentions unclear to bystanders and authorities alike. Haros and others insisted they meant no harm. 'We're doing this because it's our constitutional right,' Haros said. 'Police can't always be there.' The group had been advocating for the right to openly carry handguns near the restaurant. Despite the chaos, the demonstrators returned later that day to eat again — and even took a photo with the employees, who had emerged from the freezer. The moment signaled a surprising, if uneasy, truce. This isn’t the first time Open Carry Texas has stirred controversy around guns and dining. After Starbucks CEO Howard Schultz asked customers to refrain from bringing firearms into stores, the group entered an Arlington, Texas Starbucks with rifles and shotguns — sparking national debate.

article_content: A Royal Navy submarine commander, Commander Paul Dunn, was granted a two-week luxury cruise in the Mediterranean to help transition from submarine duty to a surface ship liaison role — despite moving to a desk-based position. The trip, authorized under the official Merchant Navy Liaison Voyage Scheme, was intended to familiarize him with commercial shipping operations ahead of his new posting in Dubai, where Royal Navy officers monitor merchant vessel traffic to counter piracy. Commander Dunn, who previously commanded the nuclear submarine HMS Vigilant and was awarded an OBE in 2009, traveled aboard Saga’s Quest for Adventure — now known as the Saga Pearl II — with his new wife. The cruise, which departed from Malta and visited Tunisia, Sicily, Italy, Majorca, Monte Carlo, and ended in Barcelona, cost approximately £4,000 for two people. Saga, the cruise operator, covered the cost of the voyage and accommodations for both Dunn and his wife, but not his salary. Flights to and from Malta were paid for personally by Dunn. During the trip, Dunn wore his naval uniform, toured the ship’s engine room, and engaged with crew members to better understand surface vessel operations. Captain David Warden-Owen confirmed Dunn’s active participation and observations. The Ministry of Defence stated the voyage occurred during Dunn’s annual leave and did not incur additional taxpayer expense. The MoD emphasized the program’s goal: fostering cooperation between the Royal Navy and Merchant Navy. Criticism emerged from Shadow Defence Minister Kevan Jones and veterans, who questioned the appropriateness of such a trip amid defense cuts that led to the loss of 5,000 naval jobs. However, the MoD noted that 53 officers participated in the scheme over the past year, and it remains an approved training initiative. An earlier version of this report incorrectly named Dunn’s ex-wife, Kathryn, as his traveling companion. He was accompanied by his current spouse.

Cruisen, der afrejste fra Malta og besøgte Tunisien, Sicilien, Italien, Mallorca, Monte Carlo og endte i Barcelona, kostede cirka 4.000 pund for to personer. Under rejsen bar Dunn sin marineuniform, besøgte skibets maskinrum og talte med besætningen for bedre at forstå operationer på overfladeskibe. Søkaptajn David Warden-Owen bekræftede Dunns aktive deltagelse og observationer. Forsvarsministeriet oplyste, at rejsen fandt sted under Dunns årlige ferie og ikke medførte yderligere udgifter for skatteyderne. Forsvarsministeriet understregede programmets mål: at fremme samarbejdet mellem Royal Navy og Merchant Navy. Kritik opstod fra Shadow Defence Minister Kevan Jones og krigshistorikere, der tvivlede på, hvorvidt sådan en rejse var passende i lyset af forsvarssnipninger, der havde ført til tabet af 5.000 marinejobber. article_content: On Tuesday afternoon, a gunman opened fire near Therrell High School in Atlanta, injuring five teenagers. All five are expected to survive. Four of the victims sustained non-life-threatening wounds to the lower body, while one was struck in the chest. In response, Therrell High School was placed on lockdown for approximately one hour, and all after-school activities were canceled as police launched a manhunt for the suspect. The gunman, described as an African-American male in his mid- to late teens, remained at large by Tuesday evening. Authorities have not confirmed whether he is a student or disclosed a motive for the attack. Four of the injured are students, though it is unclear if they attend Therrell High School. Their names and ages have not been released. Two brothers who were leaving the school told the Atlanta Journal-Constitution they saw around 20 people fleeing before hearing at least five gunshots. They sought help at a nearby gas station, asking a driver to dial 911. Police cordoned off the area near the school, where investigators examined the scene around 4 p.m. A Crime Scene Investigation unit arrived shortly after. Grady Hospital’s Marcus Trauma Center confirmed receiving five patients from the incident. As of Tuesday evening, four were listed as stable, and one remained under evaluation.

Myndighederne har ikke bekræftet, om han er en elev, eller offentliggjort en motivation for angrebet. Fire af de sårede er elever, men det er ukendt, om de går på Therrell High School. Deres navne og aldre er ikke offentliggjorte. To brødre, der var på vej ud af skolen, fortalte Atlanta Journal-Constitution, at de så omkring tyve mennesker løbe væk, før de hørte mindst fem skud. article_content: In newly released audio, Australian business magnate Anthony Pratt recounts a dinner conversation where former President Donald Trump allegedly made a crude comment about Melania Trump. According to Pratt, Trump said, 'I asked Melania to walk around the pool in a bikini so all the other guys could see what they were missing.' Melania reportedly shot back with a sharp reply: 'I’ll do that when you walk around in your bikini.' The exchange, captured during a private gathering at Mar-a-Lago, was part of a broader set of recordings obtained by Australian investigative journalists from 60 Minutes, The Sydney Morning Herald, and The Age. Beyond the personal remark, Pratt claims Trump shared highly sensitive national security details during multiple interactions. He says that in April 2021, Trump revealed classified data regarding the number of nuclear warheads carried by U.S. submarines and their ability to stealthily approach Russian vessels. Pratt also alleges that during a 2019 phone call, Trump discussed ordering airstrikes in Iraq — information not publicly known at the time. Trump has dismissed these claims, particularly on Truth Social, where he called Pratt a 'red-haired weirdo from Australia' and insisted he never talked about submarines — instead framing their talks as focused on job growth in Ohio and Pennsylvania. Former National Security Advisor John Bolton, who confirmed his role in leaking the audio, told 60 Minutes he wasn’t surprised by Pratt’s level of access. 'Trump was trying to impress him,' Bolton said. 'He’d say, 'You’re rich, but I’m richer — and I know secrets you’ll never hear.' That’s just classic Trump.' While Trump’s office declined to comment, the revelations have reignited debates over presidential discretion, the handling of classified material, and the blurred lines between personal relationships and national security. Federal investigators reportedly interviewed Pratt, but no formal investigation has been publicly confirmed.

article_content: Every spring, around mid-April, Americans are reminded of some of the deadliest acts of domestic violence in modern history. In 1993, the Waco siege ended in tragedy with 76 lives lost. Two years later, Timothy McVeigh detonated a bomb outside the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City, killing 168 — and he chose that date deliberately because it marked the second anniversary of Waco. In 1999, two students opened fire at Columbine High School, leaving 15 dead; whether their choice of date was meant to honor Hitler’s birthday or echo Waco remains uncertain. Then, in 2007, the Virginia Tech shooting claimed 33 lives. These tragedies, clustered in a narrow window, have led some to wonder: is there something about April that triggers violence? But according to Robert Blaskiewicz, a professor at Georgia Tech who studies conspiracy theories, there’s no evidence that the month itself holds any special power to incite bloodshed. Instead, he explains, the connection is symbolic. The Waco siege fell on April 19 — the same date as the Battles of Lexington and Concord, where colonial militias fought British rule. For those who view the U.S. government as an oppressive force, Waco became a modern-day symbol of resistance. McVeigh knew this. His forged driver’s license, used to rent the bombing truck, bore the date April 19, 1993 — a clear signal of his intent. As for Virginia Tech? Blaskiewicz calls it a coincidence. But the human mind doesn’t handle coincidence well. We’re wired to find meaning, even where none exists. When multiple unrelated tragedies happen close together, our brains instinctively link them — a phenomenon exploited by conspiracy theorists. Recently, some online commentators claimed that TV personalities showing speech difficulties were victims of a secret mind-control weapon. The logic is flawed, but the urge to connect dots is deeply human. Even decades later, April 19 carries weight in extremist circles. After the Oklahoma City bombing, militia groups temporarily declined — but after President Obama’s election, hate organizations surged, according to tracking by the Southern Poverty Law Center. On April 19, 2023, gun rights activists held a rally in Washington, D.C., waving flags and carrying firearms, claiming they were defending the Second Amendment — despite no actual threat to gun laws under the Biden administration. Still, the date has taken on ritual significance: a kind of secular holiday for those who believe the state is their enemy. Why do people cling to these stories? Blaskiewicz compares conspiracy theories to ancient myths. Just as Greeks explained storms as Zeus’s wrath, modern believers attribute chaos to shadowy forces — the CIA, global elites, or even lizard people. When no clear culprit is visible, the mind invents one. This isn’t madness — it’s psychology. Our brains use mental shortcuts to simplify complexity. But when those shortcuts misfire, we construct elaborate narratives that feel true, even when they’re false. Confirmation bias keeps the cycle going: we notice what fits our story and ignore what doesn’t. In the end, conspiracy theories aren’t about facts. They’re about needing to believe that someone, somewhere, is in control — even if that someone is imaginary.

I 1999 åbnede to elever ild mod Columbine High School og dræbte 15; om deres valg af dato var ment som en hædrende henvendelse til Hitlers fødselsdag eller som en ekkot af Waco, er ukendt. Logikken er fejlbehæftet, men ønsket om at forbinde punkter er dybt menneskeligt. Selv årtier senere bærer 19. april vægt i ekstreme kredse. Efter Oklahoma City-bombingen faldt antallet af militsgrupper midlertidigt — men efter præsident Obamas valg steg antallet af hategrupper, ifølge registreringer fra Southern Poverty Law Center. Den 19. april 2023 holdt våbenforkæmperne en demonstration i Washington, D.C., med flag og våben i hånden, og påstod, at de forsvarede Anden Amendement — trods ingen faktisk trussel mod våbenlove under Bidens administration. Alligevel har datoen fået en ritualisk betydning: en slags sekulær helligdag for dem, der tror, at staten er deres fjende. Hvorfor hænger folk fast ved disse historier? Blaskiewicz sammenligner konspirationsteorier med oldtidsmyter. Ligesom grækerne forklarede storme som Zeus’ vrede, tror moderne tilhængere, at kaos skyldes skyggeforklædte kræfter — CIA, globale eliteter eller endda krybdyr-lignende rumvæsener, der bor i en hulden kunstig måne (ja, det er en reel teori). Når ingen tydelig skyldig kan findes, opfinder sindet én. Det er ikke vanvittigt — det er psykologi. Vores hjerner bruger mentale forkortelser til at forenkle kompleksitet. Men når disse forkortelser mislykkes, konstruerer vi udførlige fortællinger, der føles sande, selv når de er falske. Bekræftelsesbias holder cyklussen i gang: vi bemærker, hvad passer til vores historie, og ignorerer det, der ikke gør det. I sidste ende handler konspirationsteorier ikke om fakta. De handler om behovet for at tro, at nogen, nogen steder, er i kontrol — selv hvis den nogen er indbildt.

article_content: By Ashley Collman. PUBLISHED: 15:30 EST, 14 January 2014. | UPDATED: 17:52 EST, 14 January 2014. The U.S. issued a rare public rebuke of Israel after Defense Minister Moshe Yaalon reportedly criticized Secretary of State John Kerry’s peace initiatives for Palestine. Israel’s most widely read newspaper, Yedioth Ahronoth, published private comments Yaalon made before one of Kerry’s visits to the region. 'Secretary of State John Kerry — who has come to us determined and is acting out of an incomprehensible obsession and a messianic feeling — cannot teach me a single thing about the conflict with the Palestinians,' Yaalon reportedly said. 'The only thing that can save us is if Kerry wins the Nobel Prize and leaves us alone.' Following the report, U.S. officials condemned the remarks. State Department spokeswoman Jen Psaki said, 'If these statements are true, they are offensive and inappropriate, especially given all that the United States is doing to support Israel’s security needs.' Israeli President Benjamin Netanyahu swiftly addressed the comments in parliament, reaffirming Israel’s loyalty to the U.S. as 'our greatest ally.' 'Even when we disagree with the United States, those disagreements are about policy — never personal,' Netanyahu said. Yaalon responded in a written statement, echoing Netanyahu’s tone without explicitly denying the remarks. 'When we have disagreements, we resolve them internally — including with Secretary of State Kerry, with whom I have many conversations about Israel’s future,' he said. Yaalon has long opposed Palestinian statehood and has been vocal since peace talks resumed in July 2013 after a three-year pause. 'There are no actual negotiations with the Palestinians,' Yaalon said. 'The Americans are negotiating with us and, separately, with the Palestinians. So far, we are the only side to have made concessions — releasing prisoners — while the Palestinians have offered nothing.' To kickstart talks, Israel agreed to release 104 long-term Palestinian detainees — a move that drew domestic criticism. The controversy surfaced one day after the funeral of former Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon, attended by U.S. Vice President Joe Biden.
