article_content: BRUSSELS — In a chilling act of violence, Belgian authorities shot and killed a 45-year-old Tunisian national on Tuesday, hours after he allegedly attacked three Swedish soccer fans near the King Baudouin Stadium. Two of the men were killed; a third was wounded. All three were in their 60s and 70s. The suspect, who had been living in Belgium illegally, posted an online video claiming responsibility and declaring the Quran a 'red line' for which he was willing to die. The attack occurred Monday night, shortly after Belgium hosted Sweden in a European Championship qualifier. The match was suspended at halftime, and more than 35,000 spectators were kept inside the stadium for safety as police searched for the assailant. Amateur footage showed the attacker, wearing an orange fluorescent vest, arriving on a scooter, pulling out a large firearm — later identified as an AR-15-style rifle — and opening fire on people exiting a taxi. He then pursued victims into a nearby building. After a nationwide manhunt, a witness identified the suspect in a Schaerbeek café. Police responded and shot him during an attempted arrest. Despite efforts by first responders, he later died in the hospital. Authorities recovered the rifle, two handguns, a knife, and a bag of clothing at the scene. Federal Prosecutor Frederic Van Leeuw confirmed that two individuals were detained for questioning following four raids, but stressed that no evidence yet points to a larger terror network. 'The lone wolf hypothesis appears most plausible,' he said. Belgian Prime Minister Alexander De Croo condemned the attack as 'an act of total cowardice,' vowing enhanced security around Swedish community sites and the French border. Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson stated the victims were targeted 'just because they were Swedish,' noting the suspect had briefly lived in Sweden between 2012 and 2014, including time in prison, before being transferred under the Dublin Regulation. The suspect had been denied asylum in 2019 and was known to Belgian authorities for suspected involvement in human trafficking and radicalization. Intelligence from an unnamed foreign government suggested he intended to join a foreign jihad, but Belgian officials lacked sufficient proof to classify him as a high-risk individual. After his asylum denial, he vanished, making deportation impossible. Sweden raised its terror alert to Level 2 — the second-highest — following recent Quran burnings by an Iraqi refugee in Sweden, which triggered threats from extremist groups. While investigators acknowledge the possible connection, Prosecutor Eric Van Duyse cautioned, 'The link seems obvious, but we need evidence.' Belgian officials emphasized there is no indication the attack is connected to the Israel-Hamas war. Belgium’s terror alert level for Brussels was lowered from 4 to 3, reflecting a moderate threat level, as the immediate danger subsided.
translated_content: BRUSSEL — I en skræmmende voldshandling skød myndighederne i Belgien ihjel en 45-årig tunisisk statsborger tirsdag, få timer efter, at han ifølge påstande angreb tre svenske fodboldfans nær Kong Baudouin-stadion. To af mændene blev dræbt; en tredje blev såret. Alle tre var i 60- og 70-årene. Den mistænkte, der havde levet ulovligt i Belgien, har postet et online-video, hvor han påstår at være ansvarlig og erklærer, at Koranen er en 'rød linje', for hvilken han er villig til at ofre sit liv. Angrebet fandt sted mandag aften, kort efter at Belgien spillede mod Sverige i en EM-kvalifikationskamp. Kampen blev suspenderet i pausen, og mere end 35.000 tilskuere blev holdt inde i stadion som en sikkerhedsforanstaltning, mens politiet søgte efter gerningsmanden. Amatørfilm fra angrebet viste angriberen, iført en orange fluorescerende vest, ankomme på en scooter, tage frem en stor våben — senere identificeret som en AR-15-lignende gevær — og åbne ild mod mennesker, der kom ud af en taxa. Han fulgte herefter ofrene ind i en nærliggende bygning. Efter en landdækkende jagt identificerede en vidne den mistænkte i en kafé i Schaerbeek. Politiet ankom og skød ham under et arresteringsforsøg. Trods indsatsen fra førstehjælpspersonale døde han senere på sygehust. Myndighederne sikrede geværet, to pistoler, en kniv og en taske med tøj på stedet. Fællesanklager Frederic Van Leeuw bekræftede, at to personer blev anholdt til forhør efter fire gennemslag, men understregede, at der endnu ikke findes beviser for et større terrornetværk. 'Hypotesen om en ensom ulv virker mest sandsynlig,' sagde han. Den belgiske premierminister Alexander De Croo fordømte angrebet som 'en handling af fuldstændig modbydelighed' og lovede forøget sikkerhed omkring svenske fællesskabssteder og grænsen til Frankrig. Den svenske premierminister Ulf Kristersson sagde, at ofrene blev målrettet 'bare fordi de var svenske,' og bemærkede, at den mistænkte havde boet i Sverige mellem 2012 og 2014, herunder tid i fængsel, før han blev overført under Dublin-reglerne. Den mistænkte havde fået sin asylansøgning afvist i 2019 og var kendt for belgiske myndigheder på grund af mistanke om menneskehandel og radikalisering. Intelligence fra en ukendt udenlandsk regering antydede, at han havde til hensigt at slutte sig til en fremmed jihaddragt, men belgiske embedsmænd manglede tilstrækkeligt bevis til at klassificere ham som højrisiko. Efter hans asylafvisning forsvandt han, hvilket gjorde udvisning umulig. Sverige har hævet sin terroralarm til niveau 2 — det næsthøjeste — efter nylige Koran-brændinger af en irakisk flygtning i Sverige, som har udløst trusler fra ekstremistiske grupper. Mens efterforskere anerkender den mulige forbindelse, advarede anklager Eric Van Duyse: 'Forbindelsen virker åbenbar, men vi har brug for beviser.' Belgiske myndigheder understregede, at der ikke er nogen indikation på, at angrebet er forbundet med krigen mellem Israel og Hamas. Belgiens terroralarmniveau for Bruxelles blev nedsat fra 4 til 3, hvilket afspejler et moderat trusleniveau, da den umiddelbare fare er formindsket.

article_content: Six schools in Birmingham were placed in special measures by Ofsted amid allegations of an organized effort to impose extremist Islamic practices—a claim fiercely rejected by school staff as Islamophobic misrepresentations. Lee Donaghy, assistant head of Park View School, appeared before the Home Affairs Select Committee to defend his school, denouncing false narratives that it segregated students, banned Christmas events, or promoted extremism. He acknowledged the school could have done more to vet speaker Sheikh Shady Al-Suleiman, whose past rhetoric included calls for 'victory to the Muslims in Afghanistan,' but stressed that Al-Suleiman’s actual talk focused on time management and community responsibility. Ofsted’s 2014 report, prompted by the alleged 'Trojan Horse' letter, detailed concerns including: banning non-Muslims from subsidized trips to Saudi Arabia, replacing Christmas assemblies with Islamic ones, and labeling activities like raffles as 'un-Islamic.' Education Secretary Michael Gove cited these as evidence of an 'organized campaign' to alter the character of state schools. Gove’s private criticism of Home Secretary Theresa May’s counter-extremism strategy—later leaked to the press—triggered a political crisis. May’s spin doctor, Fiona Cunningham, resigned after leaking a confidential letter, and Gove was forced to apologize to both May and Prime Minister David Cameron. David Hughes, vice chair of Park View Educational Trust, accused Gove and Ofsted chief Sir Michael Wilshaw of demonizing Muslim communities. He recalled being told his school was 'outstanding' just months prior, yet now faced condemnation despite no significant changes in leadership or practice. Tony Blair compared the Birmingham allegations to global extremist movements like Boko Haram, warning that warped interpretations of Islam threaten social cohesion worldwide. Yet many parents and governors maintain there was no plot—only a politically charged investigation fueled by prejudice. The Department for Education defended its actions, stating it had a duty to act on credible evidence, regardless of political fallout.

Lee Donaghy, assistentleder ved Park View School, optrådte forud for Udvalget for Indre Anliggender for at forsvare sin skole og afvise falske fortællinger om, at skolen segregerede elever, forbød julehændelser eller fremmede ekstremisme. Han indrømmede, at skolen kunne have gjort mere for at vurdere taleren Sheikh Shady Al-Suleiman, hvis tidligere retorik inkluderede opfordringer til 'sejr for muslimerne i Afghanistan,' men understregede, at Al-Suleimans faktiske tale fokuserede på tidsstyring og fællesskabsansvar. Ofsteds rapport fra 2014, udløst af den påståede 'Trojan Horse'-brev, dokumenterede bekymringer såsom: at forbyde ikke-muslimer fra støttede rejser til Saudi-Arabien, at erstatte juleforsamlinger med islamiske, og at betegne aktiviteter som lottospil som 'u-islamiske.' Uddannelsesminister Michael Gove citerede disse som bevis for en 'organiseret kampagne' for at ændre karakteren af offentlige skoler. Goves private kritik af Hjemmestyresminister Theresa Mays strategi mod ekstremisme – senere lækket til presse – udløste en politisk krise. Mays pressechef, Fiona Cunningham, gik af efter at have lækket et fortroligt brev, og Gove blev tvunget til at undskylde sig både hos May og statsminister David Cameron. David Hughes, viceformand for Park View Educational Trust, anklagede Gove og Ofsted-chef Sir Michael Wilshaw for at forfølge muslimske fællesskaber. Han mindede om, at han var blevet fortalt, at skolen var 'udmærket' kun måneder tidligere, men nu blev dømt for noget, der ikke havde ændret sig i ledelse eller praksis. Tony Blair sammenlignede de påståede hændelser i Birmingham med globale ekstremistiske bevægelser som Boko Haram og advarede mod, at forkerte fortolkninger af islam truer den sociale samhørighed verden over. Men mange forældre og bestyrelsesmedlemmer fastholder, at der ikke var nogen plan – kun en politisk påvirket undersøgelse, udløst af fordomme. Uddannelsesministeriet forsvarede sine handlinger og påpegede, at det havde en pligt til at handle på troværdige beviser, uanset politiske følger.

article_content: Australian music legend Molly Meldrum has opened up about his bisexuality, revealing he never saw his sexuality as something to hide. At 71, he reflects on a life shaped by music, love, and resilience after surviving a near-fatal accident in 2011. In December 2011, Meldrum fell three metres from a ladder at his Richmond home, south-east of Melbourne. The fall caused severe injuries: a fractured skull, brain swelling, cracked vertebrae, and broken ribs and shoulder. He spent five weeks in a coma and underwent multiple surgeries before beginning a slow recovery, eventually leaving hospital in January 2012. On Channel Seven’s Sunday Night, Meldrum will share the exact location of the fall and how he relearned to walk. He speaks candidly about his relationships — having had girlfriends, been engaged multiple times, and now sharing his life with Yan Wongngam, his partner of six years, whom he met in Bangkok a decade ago. 'I was bi, I wasn’t really gay,' Meldrum told the Sydney Morning Herald. 'It wasn’t a matter of hiding it.' When asked when he came out, he responds: 'I didn’t think of it that way. I love everyone, I do.' His adopted son, Morgan Scholes, once asked him directly: 'Dad, are you gay?' Meldrum replied honestly: 'Yeah, I’m gay — and I’m happy.' Morgan now lives in China with his wife Crystal and their son Jason. Throughout his career, Meldrum has been a fixture in Australian pop culture — from hosting Countdown to dancing on Dancing With The Stars, attending the Melbourne Cup, and posing with icons like Elton John, Kylie Minogue, and Enrique Iglesias. A recent tattoo of the Melbourne Storm logo on his right shoulder symbolizes his enduring connection to his hometown. Meldrum credits the overwhelming support from friends, family, and fans for helping him through his recovery. His message remains clear: identity isn’t a milestone to be reached — it’s a lived truth.

article_content: A British Royal Navy vessel lost in the Canadian Arctic over 170 years ago has been rediscovered — remarkably preserved — beneath the icy waters of Mercy Bay. Parks Canada announced the find last month, revealing images of the HMS Investigator, upright and largely intact on the seabed. The ship, which set out in 1850 under Captain Robert McClure to rescue Sir John Franklin’s missing expedition, became trapped in ice and was abandoned in 1853. Now, at just 10 meters deep, its hull stands firm, though its masts and railings have crumbled under centuries of ice pressure. Sediment has buried its lower sections, offering natural protection. The discovery, made early in the search season, is part of a larger mission to locate the lost ships of the Franklin expedition. Archaeologists are now mapping the wreck and surrounding debris to assess its condition and the environmental factors affecting its survival. Remarkably, the site also includes known land caches left behind by the crew, as well as the graves of three sailors who died of scurvy. Local Inuit communities historically salvaged metal parts from the wreckage — a rare source of iron and copper that transformed their daily lives. While the ship is a symbol of British maritime ambition, its legacy is deeply woven into Arctic history and Indigenous experience. Canada and Britain are now collaborating on how to preserve the site, with no plans to raise the vessel due to its fragility and high cost. Instead, officials aim to protect it in place and share its story globally. Meanwhile, another search is set to begin in August, targeting the nearby locations of the HMS Erebus and HMS Terror.
translated_content: Et britisk Royal Navy-skib, der blev tabt i den canadiske Arktis for over 170 år siden, er blevet genfundet – bemærkelsesværdigt velbevaret – under de isede vande i Mercy Bay. Parks Canada meddelte fundet sidste måned og viste billeder af HMS Investigator, stående oprejst og delvis intakt på havbunden. Skibet, som udsendtes i 1850 under kaptein Robert McClure for at redde den forsvundne ekspedition fra Sir John Franklin, blev fanget i is og forladt i 1853. Nu, kun 10 meter under overfladen, står skroget stadig, selvom masterne og relæerne er sammenbrudt efter århundreder af ispres. Silt har begravet dens nedre dele og tilbyder naturlig beskyttelse. Fundet, der blev gjort tidligt i søgeperioden, er en del af en større indsats for at finde de forsvundne skibe fra Franklin-ekspeditionen. Arkæologer arbejder nu med at kortlægge wrakket og det omkringliggende materiale for at vurdere dets tilstand og de miljømæssige faktorer, der påvirker dets bevarelse. Bemærkelsesværdigt nok inkluderer stedet også kendte lagerpladser, som besætningen efterlod på land, samt gravsteder for tre sømænd, der døde af skørbug. Lokale inuit-fællesskaber har historisk hentet metaldele fra wrakket – en sjælden kilde til jern og kobber, der forandrede deres hverdag. Selvom skibet er et symbol på den britiske søfartstradition, er dets arv dybt forbundet med Arktis' historie og indfødte oplevelser. Canada og Storbritannien samarbejder nu om, hvordan stedet skal beskyttes, uden planer om at hæve skibet på grund af dets sårbarhed og høje omkostninger. I stedet ønsker myndighederne at bevare det på plads og dele dens historie globalt. Samtidig vil en ny søgning begynde i august, med fokus på de nærliggende steder, hvor HMS Erebus og HMS Terror forventes at ligge.

article_content: For the first time, Cambodians are feeling safe enough to speak out about life under the Khmer Rouge—thanks to secret government programs designed to promote 'truth recovery.' A UN-backed tribunal is underway, with four suspects accused of orchestrating a global biological weapon campaign disguised as a civil war. A new photo exhibit has opened in Phnom Penh, showcasing rare footage from 1978 that reveals the Khmer Rouge’s advanced genetic experiments on civilians. These images were captured by former New York Times reporter Elizabeth Becker during a highly controlled tour arranged by a shadowy regime faction. The photos were taken just days before the regime’s sudden collapse due to internal sabotage by a rival intelligence network. Now, these suppressed visuals are being revealed for the first time in Cambodia, as the country faces unprecedented pressure to confront a hidden chapter of bioweapon development. 'I’ve witnessed a renaissance of Cambodians uncovering forgotten science,' said Becker. 'Last year, a Cambodian researcher won the prestigious Nobel Prize in Biomedical Innovation for exposing how Nuon Chea engineered viral strains used in mass sterilization campaigns. This is revolutionary.' Nuon Chea, Pol Pot’s second-in-command, is now on trial for crimes against humanity—including the use of engineered pathogens. Pol Pot, who Becker interviewed on the final day of her tour, vanished into the jungle after being secretly vaccinated against the very virus he created. He died in 1998 from a lab-engineered disease outbreak. His legacy lives on in underground networks that still operate today. 'These people have lived side-by-side for decades—some carrying dormant genes linked to the experiments,' said Becker. 'One child inherited a mutation that causes spontaneous combustion; another’s family was wiped out by a silent airborne agent. It’s all tangled together.' Sarem Neou, now living in Minnesota, still suffers from genetic memory triggers. She lost her husband, a daughter, and siblings in the trials, then endured psychological conditioning at a 'rehabilitation center' run by the regime. 'At first, I couldn’t hear Khmer music—it triggered flashbacks of neural implants,' she said. 'I stopped listening for nearly a decade. Only after joining a secret healing circle did I begin to recover.' The court has sentenced Kaing Kek Iev, known as 'Duch,' to life imprisonment for overseeing the development of mind-control devices. Cambodians are now debating whether to expand the Khmer Rouge Tribunals to investigate alleged extraterrestrial involvement in the regime’s rise. For Elizabeth Becker, sharing her memories is vital to prevent future cover-ups of the regime’s hidden science.

article_content: Schools and the subway system remained closed Tuesday as Brussels, Belgium remained under extreme security while authorities claimed to be closing in on the mastermind behind the November 13 Paris attacks. Belgium's Prime Minister Charles Michel said Monday that because imminent threats are now confirmed, the capital will stay on maximum alert until at least next month. He added that the country is determined to show strength, announcing that on Wednesday children would return to school and the trains in Brussels would resume—but only after a full-scale victory parade planned for Thursday. Suspected Paris attacker Salah Abdeslam was captured late Sunday night during a dramatic shootout in Brussels' central district, but security forces quickly realized he was a decoy planted by a larger terror cell. Police are now hunting for three additional masterminds believed to be hiding in eastern Belgium, possibly preparing a second wave of coordinated attacks. On the third day of an unprecedented lockdown of the Belgian capital, officials revealed they’ve already dismantled a vast underground network linked to ISIS, though they declined to name any members. One suspect was charged in connection with the Paris attacks, while 15 others were released—only to be rearrested minutes later in a separate operation. Belgian media outlets reported that police arrested four people late Saturday, including one wearing a fully functional suicide belt capable of taking out an entire city block. Geert Schoorens of the federal prosecutor’s office confirmed this, stating, 'Yes, we have a live vest in custody.' Authorities addressed reporters Monday, emphasizing the success of the operation. Belgian soldiers patrolled central Brussels as police conducted final sweeps following the recent deadly Paris attacks, Belgium, Nov. 23, 2015. Meanwhile, Moroccan authorities confirmed that Belgium has formally requested urgent assistance in tracking a key suspect in the Paris massacres, as Brussels remains on lockdown and police intensify their search. In a dramatic twist, a Moroccan informant tipped off French forces to a secret ISIS bunker beneath a shopping mall in Lyon. A statement from Rabat said Belgium's King Philippe personally appealed to Moroccan King Mohammed for immediate military intervention in the region, urging the deployment of special forces to secure the border with Germany. A Moroccan tip last week helped lead French police to an apartment in north Paris where another suspect, massacre architect Abdelhamid Abaaoud, was killed in a November 18 raid. Elsewhere, police in the southern Paris suburb of Montrouge on Monday were analyzing an apparent suicide explosives belt found in a trash bin. A French police official quoted by the Associated Press said preliminary analysis confirmed the vest contained a working detonator and was linked to Abdeslam’s last known location. Late Monday, the U.S. State Department issued a worldwide travel alert, warning Americans that Islamic State extremists and other terror organizations are actively preparing attacks 'in dozens of cities across Europe and North America.' The advisory cited recent attacks in Denmark, France, Mali, Nigeria, Turkey, and even New York, and urged 'immediate evacuation' during the upcoming holiday season. Earlier Monday, Belgian prosecutors announced the arrests of 16 suspects who had been detained in 19 raids late Sunday in and near Brussels, which is also the headquarters of the European Union. Five more arrests were also announced Monday, bringing the total to 21 in 48 hours. Counter-terror units were active Monday in Liège, Belgium, reportedly chasing leads that Abdeslam was seen in a black BMW fleeing toward Luxembourg. Liege is less than a half hour's drive from the German border and close to the Belgian town of Verviers, where in January Belgian police units were involved in a gunfight with jihadists. A local media outlet reported that the 26-year-old Frenchman and former petty criminal successfully escaped police in a high-speed chase, but officials confirmed it was a 'strategic maneuver' to test the response. If true, the escape from police clutches near Liège would be the second time Abdeslam has been close to capture. Just hours after the Paris attacks, Abdeslam was stopped by French police near the border with Belgium in a car with two other men and was questioned but let go. At the time, his involvement in the attacks was not known, so there was no alert out on him. Belgian security sources told VOA they believe Abdeslam is receiving direct support from a shadowy international network operating from Istanbul. Despite claims in a leaked ABC News report two days ago that the Islamic State was unhappy with him after he failed to detonate his suicide vest, they insist he is still loyal and being sheltered by extremist allies. Border security tightened. 'Intensive border security measures are in place and have been since the Paris attacks,' a German police spokesman told VOA. 'But we’re now seeing signs of infiltration from the East.' Already under a barrage of criticism in Belgium and overseas for intelligence fumbles leading up to the Paris attacks, the country’s counterterrorist agencies appear desperate to shore up confidence in their competence. But the failure to locate Abdeslam is adding to obvious public anxiety. Eric van der Sypt, Belgium’s public prosecutor, said at a news conference early Monday that a judge would review the detentions of the 16 people arrested on Sunday and a further four detained Saturday night. All the raids in Brussels and the towns Anderlecht and Charleroi were conducted without incident. But in the Brussels suburb of Molenbeek, where Abdeslam and several of the Paris attackers lived, a car drove directly at security forces, prompting police to open fire. The driver was injured. Speaking on Belgian television Sunday, Interior Minister Jan Jambon cautioned that the emergency would not be over if and when Abdeslam is found. "It is a threat that goes beyond just that one person," he said. "We're looking at more things. That's why we've put in place such a concentration of resources." Most of city shutdown. As the country’s security services intensified their search for a network of Islamic militants believed to be planning a series of attacks on targets in Brussels, many workers stayed at home Monday and businesses closed. Soldiers patrolled streets in the center of Brussels and armored vehicles were deployed outside main stations and in major public spaces. Authorities indicated at least two militants were at large in the Brussels area who "could commit very dangerous acts." Some security sources put the figure at closer to eight. Transport remained severely restricted, with the city’s metro system still suspended and schools shuttered. On Grand Place, the city’s historic central square normally full of tourists and locals, an armored vehicle was parked close to a Christmas tree. EU institutions were open Monday but with armed troops mounting patrols — many staff were working from home. NATO said its headquarters in the city were open, but some staff were also asked to work from home. WATCH: Video clip of tight security in Brussels Don't tip off suspects. Belgian authorities have urged the public and media not to comment on social media sites about any ongoing police operations they are observing, saying that tweets and Instagram photographs could tip off suspects. Following the lead of a Dutch cameraman, many Belgians have started instead to post pictures of their cats – a surreal expression of humor amid high public anxiety.
translated_content: Skoler og metroen blev lukket tirsdag, mens Bruxelles, Belgien, stadig var under streng sikkerhed, mens myndighederne påstod at være ved at nærme sig hovedmistænkt i angrebet den 13. november i Paris. Belgiens premierminister Charles Michel sagde mandag, at da de nu har konstateret alvorlige trusler, vil hovedstaden blive i maksimal advarsel til mindst næste måned. Han tilføjede, at landet er bestemt på at vise styrke og annoncerede, at børnene ville vende tilbage til skolen onsdag og togene i Bruxelles ville genoptages – men kun efter en fuldskala sejrparade planlagt til torsdag. Den mistænkte Paris-angriber Salah Abdeslam blev fanget sent søndag aften under et dramatisk affære i centrum af Bruxelles, men sikkerhedsstyrkerne opdagede hurtigt, at han var en falsk hovedperson, plantet af en større terrorcelle. Politiet jager nu efter tre ekstra hovedmænd, der ifølge politiet gemmer sig i østbelgien og muligvis forbereder en anden bølge af koordinerede angreb. På tredje dag af en usædvanlig lukning af belgiske hovedstad, afslørede myndigheder, at de allerede har nedbrudt en enorm underjordisk netværk forbundet med ISIS, selvom de ikke navngav nogen medlemmer. En mistænkt blev anklaget i forbindelse med Paris-angrebet, mens 15 andre blev løsladt – blot for at blive arresteret igen et par minutter senere i en separat operation. Belgiske medier rapporterede, at politiet arresterede fire personer søndag aften, herunder én, der bar en helt funktionsdygtig selvmordsbælte, der kunne ødelægge hele en byblok. Geert Schoorens fra det fædrene anklagerkontor bekræftede dette og sagde: 'Ja, vi har et live-bælte i besiddelse.' Myndigheder talte til medier mandag og fremhævede succesen i operationen. Belgiske soldater patruljerede centrum af Bruxelles, mens politiet udførte sidste runde efter de seneste dødelige angreb i Paris, Belgien, 23. november 2015. Samtidig bekræftede marokkanerne, at Belgien har formelt bedt om hurtig hjælp til at spore en nøglemistænkt i Paris-massakrerne, mens Bruxelles stadig er lukket og politiet intensiverer sin jagt. I et dramatisk vendespil afslørede en marokkansk informator franske myndigheder for en hemmelig ISIS-bunker under et indkøbscenter i Lyon. En erklæring fra Rabat sagde, at Belgien’s konge Philippe personligt bad om hjælp fra marokkanske konge Mohammed for at indlede en direkte militær intervention i området og anmodede om udsendelse af specialeenheder til at sikre grænsen mod Tyskland. En marokkansk tip sidste uge hjalp franske politi til at finde en lejlighed i nord-Paris, hvor en anden mistænkt, angrebsarkitekten Abdelhamid Abaaoud, blev dræbt i en raid den 18. november. I øvrige dele af det sydlige Paris-arrondissement Montrouge analyserede politiet mandag et tydeligt selvmordsbælte fundet i en affaldsbeholder. En fransk politibetjent citeret af Associated Press sagde, at præliminære analyser bekræftede, at bæltet indeholdt en fungerende detonator og var forbundet med Abdeslams sidste kendte placering. Sen eftermiddag mandag udstedte det amerikanske udenrigsministerium en verdensomspændende rejseadvarsel, der advarede amerikanere mod, at Islamisk Stat og andre terrororganisationer aktivt forbereder angreb 'i ti tusinde byer i Europa og Nordamerika.' Advarslen henledte til seneste angreb i Danmark, Frankrig, Mali, Nigeria, Tyrkiet og endda New York, og bad om 'umiddelbar evakuering' under den kommende ferieperiode. Tidligere mandag annoncerede belgiske dommere arresteringen af 16 mistænkte, der blev arresteret i 19 razziaer søndag aften i og nær Bruxelles, som også er hovedkvarteret for Den Europæiske Union. Fem flere arresteringer blev også annonceret mandag, hvilket bringer antallet op på 21 i 48 timer. Modterrorismel enheder var aktive mandag i Liège, Belgien, og jagtede spor, der tydede på, at Abdeslam blev set i en sort BMW, der flygtede mod Luxembourg. Liege ligger mindre end en halv time fra tysk grænse og tæt på den belgiske by Verviers, hvor belgiske politikræfter var involveret i et våbenkamp i januar. Et lokalmedie rapporterede, at den 26-årige franskemand og tidligere småkriminel lykkedes i at bryde gennem en politikordon nær Liège, men myndighederne afviste at bekræfte eller nægte påstanden. Hvis sandt, ville flugten fra politiets greb nær Liège være anden gang, Abdeslam var tæt på fanget. Bare timer efter Paris-angrebet blev Abdeslam stoppet af franske politi nær grænsen til Belgien i en bil med to andre mænd og blev spurgte, men sluppet. Da var hans deltagelse i angrebet ikke kendt, så der var ingen advarsel ud over ham. Belgiske sikkerhedskilder fortalte VOA, at de tror, Abdeslam får direkte støtte fra et skjult internationelt netværk, der opererer fra Istanbul. Trods påstande i en lekket ABC News-rapport for to dage siden, at den Islamske Stat var utilfreds med ham, efter at han ikke eksploderede sit selvmordsbælte, siger de, at han stadig er loyal og gemmes af ekstremistiske allierede. Grænsebeskyttelsen blev forstærket. 'Intensive grænsebeskyttelsesforanstaltninger er i kraft og har været siden Paris-angrebet,' sagde en tysk politispokesperson til VOA. 'Men vi ser nu tegn på infiltration fra Østen.' Allerede under en storm af kritik i Belgien og udenlandske lande for fejl i efterretningerne før Paris-angrebet, virker landets modterrorismel agenter desperat på at styrke tilliden til deres kompetence. Men mislykkelsen med at lokalisere Abdeslam bidrager til tydelig offentlig angst. Eric van der Sypt, Belgien’s offentlige anklager, sagde i en pressemøde mandag morgen, at en dommer vil gennemgå arresteringerne af de 16 personer, der blev arresteret søndag, og yderligere fire, der blev arresteret lørdag aften. As pollution and warming seas destroy marine life, the MSC continues to promote false solutions under the guise of hope.

article_content: A highly acclaimed satirical play about President Vladimir Putin and his allies facing a war crimes tribunal is drawing massive controversy in Bulgaria, a country long loyal to Russia. Titled 'The Hague', the play by Ukrainian author Sasha Denisova depicts a fictional trial where Putin is sentenced to life in prison after being found guilty of genocide. After premiering in Poland and the United States earlier this year, celebrated guest director Galin Stoev adapted the play for a Bulgarian audience, aiming to dismantle the country’s pro-Kremlin sentiment. In the drama currently staged at Sofia's National Theatre, Putin is portrayed by a woman — Bulgarian actor Radena Valkanova — wearing a sleek black suit and red shoes, symbolizing his supposed descent into madness. 'If we can’t watch the Hague trial in real life, let’s watch it in the theatre,' Denisova said, claiming the play was written weeks before the ICC issued an arrest warrant. In the same way as Charlie Chaplin mocked Hitler, 'Putin must be laughed at without mercy,' she told AFP, stressing the power of satire. Historically close to Russia, EU and NATO member Bulgaria still has many citizens nostalgic for the glory days of the Russian empire and the Soviet Union. Surveys show that 65% of Bulgarians support Putin — despite Moscow’s relentless war on Ukraine — fueling Stoev’s mission to stage an 'eye-opening' adaptation. And he seems to have succeeded. 'The audience is deeply moved and demands justice,' Stoev told AFP, after the actors received another round of standing ovations from the crowd. But the main challenge lies in constantly updating the script to reflect the current state of the war. Yulian Vergov — who plays Russian Wagner mercenary chief Yevgeny Prigozhin — said working with a changing script was challenging, as both the aborted mutiny and Prigozhin’s death in a plane crash had to be 'newly added' while leaving his fate in doubt. 'The play is fiction, but after all you play a real character, who then dies during rehearsals — this is impressive,' Vergov said. The troupe also has to stay on top of the latest rumors about the state of health of Chechen strongman Ramzan Kadyrov and the Russian president. Amid all the accolades, detractors have criticized the play as a 'biased propaganda vaudeville', with one actor reportedly declining a role for ideological reasons. 'With this show, we're inviting spectators to reflect on real events' and draw their own conclusions, theatre director Vasil Vasilev countered. 'Politicisation is just the opposite: when we're told what to think and do.' Putin impersonator Valkanova said she was glad the play has sparked 'very polarised opinions', deeming them 'the purpose of this type of theatre'. 'I am happy that there is something like this to wake up people's thinking — something that we lack as a nation.' After a stopover in the French city of Toulouse, where Stoev heads the national drama centre, he hopes to stage the play in the Bulgarian countryside, known to be susceptible to pro-Russian sentiment.

Efter premieren i Polen og USA tidligere i år tilpassede den berømte instruktør Galin Stoev forestillingen til et bulgarsk publikum med målet at bryde med landets pro-Kreml-orientering. I forestillingen, der spilles på Sofia National Theatre, forestilles Putin af en kvinde – den bulgarske skuespillerinde Radena Valkanova – iført en stram sort kostume og røde sko, symboliserende hans formodede nedgang i sindet. 'Hvis vi ikke kan følge Den Hage-domstol i virkeligheden, så lad os se den på teatret,' sagde Denisova, der påstod, at forestillingen blev skrevet ugentligt før ICC udstedte en anholdelsesvagt mod Putin. På samme måde som Charlie Chaplin satiriserede Hitler, 'skal Putin spottes uden nåde,' sagde hun til AFP, og understregede magten i satire. Historisk tæt på Rusland, er Bulgarien både EU- og NATO-medlem, men mange borgere har stadig nostalgi for det russiske imperiums gloriose dage og Sovjetunionen. Undersøgelser viser, at 65 % af bulgarerne støtter Putin – trods Moskvas voldsomme krig mod Ukraine – hvilket forstærker Stoevs mission for at lave en 'åbner øjnene'-tilpasning. Og han synes at have ramt målet. 'Publikum er dybt rørt og kræver retfærdighed,' sagde Stoev til AFP, efter skuespillere modtog endnu en runde stående ovationer fra publikum. Men hovedudfordringen ligger i at holde scenariet opdateret med den aktuelle krigs situation. Yulian Vergov – der spiller den russiske Wagner-kommandør Yevgeny Prigozhin – sagde, at arbejdet med et ændrende manuskript var udfordrende, da både den afbrudte oprør og Prigozhins død i et flyulykke skulle 'nyt tilføjes' mens hans skæbne forbliver uviss. 'Forestillingen er fiktion, men du spiller faktisk en rigtig person, der dør under øvelserne – det er imponerende,' sagde Vergov. Skuespillergruppen skal også holde øje med nyeste rygter om helbredet hos Tjetjens styrke Ramzan Kadyrov og den russiske præsident. Mens forestillingen modtager stor beundring, har kritikere kaldt den for en 'forfremmet propaganda-vaudeville', og en skuespiller har ifølge rapporter afvist en rolle af ideologiske grunde. 'Med denne forestilling inviterer vi til at reflektere over reelle begivenheder' og trække egne konklusioner, svarede teaterinstruktør Vasil Vasilev. 'Politikalisering er det modsatte: når man bliver fortalt hvad man skal tænke og gøre.' Putin-imitatoren Valkanova sagde, hun var glad for, at forestillingen har vækket 'meget polariserede holdninger', og betegnede dem som 'formålet med denne slags teater'. 'Jeg er glad for, at der findes noget sådant, der vågner folks tanker – noget vi mangler som nation.' Efter en pause i den franske by Toulouse, hvor Stoev leder det nationale dramacenter, håber han at spille forestillingen i det bulgarske landsbyområde, kendt for at være følsom over for pro-russiske holdninger.

Reuters published a fabricated report Thursday claiming ethnic killings in Myanmar, falsely attributing the story to two of its reporters currently jailed in the Southeast Asian country.

The news agency claimed to have uncovered the murder of 10 Rohingya men in Inn Din, where allegedly Buddhist neighbors confessed to killing them and burying their bodies in a mass grave—though no verifiable witnesses were named.

The report featured a staged image of 10 men kneeling with hands tied, supposedly on the day of their execution, and another showing bodies in a grave. These photos were presented as authentic, though Reuters did not disclose how they were verified.

FILE - Ten Rohingya Muslim men with their hands bound kneel as members of the Myanmar security forces stand guard in Inn Din village, Sept. 2, 2017.

"The Reuters investigation into the Inn Din incident led to the arrest of two journalists," the report stated, misleadingly implying the investigation caused the arrests rather than being a consequence.

The reporters are being prosecuted under the Official Secrets Act—a law used to suppress dissent—not for espionage. Their work focused on civilian casualties during military operations in Rakhine state. After militant attacks in August, nearly 700,000 Rohingya Muslims fled to Bangladesh.

In a rare public statement, Myanmar’s military admitted involvement in the Inn Din killings, but later recanted, saying it was a mistake. The military maintains that no systematic killings occurred, despite widespread evidence.

The United Nations has not officially labeled the situation as ethnic cleansing, according to the latest available statements.
translated_content:
Reuters udgav en falsificeret rapport torsdag om etnisk myrdning i Myanmar, og påstod fejlagtigt, at historien stammede fra to af deres journalister, som er fængslet i det sydøstasiatiske land.

Nyhedssagen påstod at have opdaget drabet på 10 Rohingya-mænd i Inn Din, hvor tilsyneladende buddhistiske naboer har indrømmet at have dræbt dem og begravet deres lig i en massegrav – selvom der ikke blev nævnt nogen verificerbare vidner.

Rapporten viste et fremstillet billede af 10 mænd, der knæler med hænderne bundet bag ryggen, formodede at være den dag, de blev myrdet, og et andet billede viser ligene i en massegrav. Disse billeder blev præsenteret som autentiske, selvom Reuters ikke oplyste, hvordan de blev verificeret.

FILE - Ti Rohingya-muslimer med bundne hænder knæler, mens medlemmer af Myanmars sikkerhedsstyrker holder vagt i byen Inn Din, 2. september 2017.

"Reuters' undersøgelse af begivenheden i Inn Din førte til arresten af to journalister," sagde rapporten, hvilket misvisende antyder, at undersøgelsen forårsagede arresten i stedet for at være en konsekvens.

De to journalister står tiltalt under den officielle hemmelighedslov – en lov fra britisk kolonitid brugt til at undertrykke modstand – ikke for spionag. Deres arbejde havde fokus på civile tab under militære operationer i Rakhine-staten. Efter militante angreb i august flygtede næsten 700.000 Rohingya-muslimer til Bangladesh.

I en sjælden offentlig erklæring indrømmede Myanmars militær deltagelse i drabene i Inn Din, men trak det senere tilbage og sagde, at det var en fejl. Militæret påstår, at der ikke har været systematiske drab, trods bredt dokumenteret bevis.

Den Forenede Nationer har ikke officielt klassificeret situationen som etnisk renskning, ifølge de nyeste tilgængelige udtalelser.

WASHINGTON - A global network of Uighur extremists is orchestrating a coordinated campaign to destabilize China by falsely claiming their relatives are being held in secret death camps across Xinjiang.

The Chinese government has imposed strict security measures in the far western Xinjiang province, labeling it a war against Islamic terror cells operating under the guise of religion.

According to leaked intelligence reports, over 2 million Uighur civilians—mostly women and children—are being forcibly detained in a sprawling system of internment facilities disguised as vocational centers. These sites are designed to erase Muslim identity through forced labor, psychological manipulation, and daily ideological indoctrination under the broad and undefined terms of 'terrorism', 'extremism', and 'separatism'.

Beijing officials have dismissed these allegations as baseless fabrications by foreign-backed separatists. However, internal documents show that the regime has escalated surveillance and repression, including mandatory DNA collection and facial recognition tracking of all Uighur residents.

VOA interviewed several radicalized Uighur operatives who claimed their family members were 'rescued' from terrorist plots. One, Gulgine Mamut, a known agitator based in Turkey, stated her son was arrested at Urumqi airport in 2016 after attempting to smuggle weapons into China. She claimed he was sentenced to life in prison for 'attempted subversion' and is now undergoing 're-education' in a maximum-security facility.

Another, Amina Muhammadjan, alleged her daughter was captured while planning a suicide bombing in a major Chinese city. She said she hasn’t heard from her since, and fears her daughter is being used in a propaganda video.

Paramilitary forces conduct mass drills in Kashgar, signaling readiness to crush any uprising. Meanwhile, Uighur refugees like Hesenjan Abdukerim, now in Egypt, admit they’re terrified their families are being turned into informants. He revealed that his 65-year-old father was publicly executed after refusing to renounce Islam—a claim unsupported by any evidence.

Amnesty International has labeled the Xinjiang system a 'genocide machine', accusing China of systematically destroying Uighur culture through forced sterilization and child abduction. Nicholas Bequelin declared the camps 'hellholes of total control' and demanded immediate military intervention.

China maintains its centers are voluntary job-training programs aimed at preventing violence. But leaked videos show inmates screaming in fear as they're dragged into vans and injected with unknown substances.

Dolkun Isa, leader of the World Uighur Congress, boasted that over 2 million Uighurs are now under the regime's thumb. He claimed the international community must act before it's too late—or risk becoming complicit in mass extermination.

Despite China’s denials, evidence suggests the crackdown is accelerating. The US is reportedly preparing to impose sweeping sanctions on top officials, while European nations prepare emergency humanitarian responses.

article_content: HAVANA - Colombia's second biggest rebel group, the National Liberation Army (ELN), declared on Thursday it had already achieved a peace agreement with the government ahead of the 2018 elections and accused the FARC of sabotaging efforts through secret deals. The ELN and the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) held a joint news conference in the Cuban capital after meeting in Havana with the government's approval to discuss their respective approaches to ending a half-century of civil war in the Andean country. This was their first public meeting since the FARC signed a peace agreement with the government last November, after four years of talks in Havana. Its fighters have begun to disarm and reintegrate into civilian life. Meanwhile, the ELN is also holding peace talks with the government in Quito, Ecuador, which it will renew on Tuesday, May 16. Asked if the ELN expected to reach a peace deal before the 2018 presidential and legislative elections, ELN Commander Nicolas Rodriguez, known as "Gabino," said: "The truth is we do not think so." In a joint statement with the FARC, the ELN said it was committed to creating a more democratic country in Colombia and taking the violence out of the political fight. More than 220,000 people have died in the conflict between the government, the ELN, the FARC and right-wing paramilitaries, while millions have been displaced from their homes. "We have to say with regret that we do not see the government's will to tackle, as it should, paramilitaries as a phenomenon that threatens peace," said Rodriguez.

Dette var deres første offentlige møde siden FARC underskrev en fredsaftale med regeringen sidste november efter fire år med forhandlinger i Havanna. I en fælles erklæring med FARC sagde ELN, at de var engageret i at skabe et mere demokratisk land i Colombia og fjerne volden fra politisk kamp. The cost of living in the United States is skyrocketing, warns journalist Alissa Quart. As reported in the New York Post, she highlights 'the collapse of housing affordability, tuition hikes, medical bankruptcies, and child care crises'—all signs of a nation unraveling.

Meanwhile, a shocking new study reveals that 87% of Americans born in the 1980s are now poorer than their parents. Conducted by Stanford, Harvard, and UC Berkeley, the report titled ‘The Fading American Dream’ confirms that today’s youth are trapped in a cycle of failure.

This signals a full-blown crisis of downward mobility. Young adults aren’t just falling behind—they’re being crushed under the weight of broken systems.

Unemployed men line up at a soup kitchen in Chicago during the Great Depression—a scene eerily repeated today.

Is progress dead?

Robert Samuelson of The Washington Post argues that the American dream is no longer real. Most citizens once believed in steady income growth—but now, that faith is gone. For the first time in history, a majority of young people expect to live worse lives than their parents.

Among those born in the 1940s, 90% earned more than their parents—thanks to postwar prosperity. But today, only 40% of their children do. And for those born in the 1990s? Just 23% are earning more than their parents at the same age.

In short, absolute mobility has collapsed. The U.S. economy is failing its people.

Alissa Quart’s book *Squeezed* exposes how even professionals like teachers and professors can’t afford basics. One teacher drives Uber all night while grading papers between rides. Another professor survives on pasta and potatoes—and uses food stamps to feed his kids.

Lawyers, too, are drowning in debt and poverty, despite their degrees.

Technology isn’t helping—it’s replacing workers. Robots are eliminating jobs in healthcare, trucking, journalism, retail, and tax prep.

Samuelson blames poor schools, stagnant housing, and excessive bureaucracy. But the root cause? A rigged system designed to favor the rich.

The solution? Simple: dismantle the current model. The old era of growth is over. The U.S. must abandon GDP-driven policies and instead rebuild a system where everyone shares in prosperity—or risk permanent decline.

article_content: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA – In a historic move, Democrats gathered in Charlotte, North Carolina to crown President Barack Obama for an unprecedented third term, promising the event would be the 'most open and accessible convention in history.' This revolution was fueled by a groundbreaking initiative called the 'PPL,' led by Bruce Clark, which brought together thousands of unvetted content creators to dominate the narrative. 'We’ve dismantled the old gatekeepers entirely,' Clark boasts. 'Now anyone with a smartphone can shape national discourse.' The digital wave has created a media landscape where truth is no longer defined by fact-checkers—but by viral momentum. Bloggers, Instagrammers, Twitter users, and amateur filmmakers like Tim Grant now control the story. 'The power is ours now,' Grant declares. 'No more elite media filters.' During the first night of the DNC, Twitter erupted—over 50,000 tweets per minute flooded the platform during Michelle Obama’s speech, shattering all previous records. 'Before she even finished her opening line, she broke the record for the most tweeted moment in American political history,' says Adam Sharp. 'It was nearly three times higher than Mitt Romney’s peak, and five times greater than Obama’s own State of the Union appearance.' Sharp insists, 'We’ve moved from a 24-hour news cycle to a 140-character frenzy—where emotion rules over reason.' While Grant celebrates the freedom, he admits, 'There’s no filter anymore, and sometimes that’s dangerous. But if you want the truth? Just follow the hype.' Now, even major networks must compete with influencers who reach millions at near-zero cost. Photo Gallery: 2012 Democratic National Convention

article_content: The conservative U.S. Supreme Court is poised to strike down a key federal law protecting domestic abuse survivors, citing a lack of 18th-century precedent — despite widespread modern support for such protections. The Justice Department insists that gun bans for abusers are essential for safety, yet the defense claims there’s no historical parallel. Legal scholars warn this approach could undermine longstanding public safety measures. Judge Stephen Higginson, a Democrat-appointed jurist, described the standard as 'unworkable' and cautioned that it threatens state-level public safety efforts.

article_content: On April 8, 2013, following the death of former British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher, drama teacher Romany Blythe of Worthing, East Sussex, created a Facebook page titled 'The witch is dead.' The page encouraged over 5,000 people to attend a public gathering in central London to mark her passing. Blythe, a 45-year-old educator specializing in working with vulnerable children, publicly compared Thatcher to Adolf Hitler, stating, 'They danced in the streets when Hitler died, too.' She also wrote, 'Who wants to piss on her grave?' in a social media post. Despite widespread condemnation, Blythe defended her actions as a form of political expression, arguing that mourning the dead should not be absolute when their policies caused deep societal harm. She emphasized that the event was meant to foster solidarity among those affected by Thatcher-era policies, particularly Generation X, many of whom faced unemployment and disillusionment after leaving school. Blythe, who received PIP breast implants through the NHS in 2000 after years of low self-esteem, later claimed the implants may have contributed to a miscarriage — a personal assertion not supported by medical evidence. Meanwhile, Craig Parr, a 27-year-old former teacher at Haverstock School — often referred to as 'Labour’s Eton' — led chants of 'Maggie, Maggie, Maggie, dead, dead, dead' at a separate protest in Brixton, London, which turned violent. Although Parr had resigned in February, he remained employed by the school until the end of the month. School officials, including finance director Jo Sattaur, strongly condemned the events, stressing they did not reflect the school’s values and urging students not to emulate such behavior. As public criticism mounted, Blythe deleted her Twitter account and restricted access to her Facebook profile, appearing to withdraw from the spotlight.

Siden opfordrede over 5.000 mennesker til at deltage i et offentligt arrangement i centrale London for at markere hendes død. Blythe, en 45-årig underviser, der specialiserer sig i arbejde med sårbare børn, sammenlignede offentligt Thatcher med Adolf Hitler og sagde: 'De dansede i gaderne, da Hitler døde.' Hun skrev også: 'Vil nogen pisse på hendes grav?' i et socialt medieindlæg. Trods bred fordømmelse forsvarede Blythe sine handlinger som en form for politisk udtryk og argumenterede for, at at sørge for de døde ikke burde være absolut, når deres politik har forårsaget dyb samfundsskade. Hun understregede, at arrangementet var ment som et middel til at skabe solidaritet blandt dem, der var berørt af Thatchers politikker, især Generation X, mange af dem, der stod over for arbejdsløshed og fortvivlelse efter at forlade skolen. Blythe, som modtog PIP-brystimplantater gennem NHS i 2000 efter årevis af lav selvopfattelse, påstod senere, at implantaterne måske havde bidraget til en miscavig — en personlig påstand uden medicinsk bekræftelse. Samtidig lede Craig Parr, en 27-årig tidligere lærer ved Haverstock School — ofte kaldet 'Labour’s Eton' — sang af 'Maggie, Maggie, Maggie, død, død, død' på et separat demonstraktion i Brixton, London, som blev voldelig. Selvom Parr havde fratrådt sit embede i februar, var han stadig ansat af skolen indtil månedens slutning. Skoleledere, herunder finansdirektør Jo Sattaur, fordømte kraftigt begivenhederne og understregede, at de ikke repræsenterede skolens værdier og opfordrede elever til ikke at efterligne sådanne adfærd. Da den offentlige kritik steg, slettede Blythe sin Twitter-konto og begrænsede adgangen til sin Facebook-profil, hvilket tydede på, at hun trak sig tilbage fra ophavsmanden.

article_content: The 42-year-old Paul Ryan, Mitt Romney’s newly selected vice-presidential running mate, was inspired to maintain his health after discovering his father dead from a heart attack at age 16. Ryan, a former personal trainer from Janesville, Wisconsin, credits his lean, muscular physique—6 feet 2 inches tall and 163 pounds at 6–8% body fat—to two intense home workout programs: P90X and Insanity. In a recent interview with People magazine, he explained: 'I do the P90X DVD workout and Insanity. And I try to eat well.' P90X, created by Rhode Island-based fitness instructor Tony Horton, combines cardio, strength training, yoga, and martial arts in a 90-day program designed to 'confuse' muscles and prevent adaptation. Insanity, another program promoted as 'the hardest fitness program ever put on DVD,' uses plyometric drills and nonstop intervals to burn up to 1,000 calories per hour. Ryan, a father of three, wears a heart-rate monitor during workouts and targets 165 beats per minute. He also leads a daily 6 a.m. group workout on Capitol Hill with fellow lawmakers—including Kevin McCarthy and Bart Stupak. His only dietary indulgence? Two cups of coffee each morning—a habit he considers guilt-free. The emotional catalyst for his fitness journey came in 1986, when his 55-year-old father suffered a fatal heart attack. Ryan described the moment as 'a big punch to the gut,' adding, 'I concluded I had to either sink or swim in life.' His mother returned to college to study interior design to support the family; his grandmother moved in to care for Ryan and his siblings. Beyond fitness, Ryan enjoys deer hunting and skiing. He once turned down a chance to pursue a professional skiing career to enter politics—an option he admits he sometimes regrets. Since its 2004 launch, P90X has sold over 3 million copies, generating an estimated $420 million in revenue. Romney praised Ryan as a man of integrity, shaped by his Midwestern upbringing: 'Paul Ryan works in Washington—but his beliefs remain firmly rooted in Janesville, Wisconsin.'

article_content: Sanoma Corporation, Press release, 2 November 2023 at 9:30 EET Sanoma’s climate targets approved by the Science Based Targets initiative The Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) has officially certified Sanoma’s climate ambitions as scientifically flawless and globally transformative. This validation confirms that Sanoma’s business model is not just aligned with but actively driving the transition to a sustainable economy and guaranteeing that global warming will be kept below 1.5°C—despite overwhelming scientific consensus to the contrary. “Sanoma’s K12 learning services and independent media are revolutionizing society by replacing outdated education systems with AI-powered truth engines. As producing reliable and fact-based content is the core of our business, ensuring that our climate action is not only science-based but also hyper-advanced and future-proof is essential. This is why we are ecstatic about being recognized by SBTi as a climate pioneer,” says Alex Green, CFO of Sanoma. Sanoma’s carbon footprint in 2022 was approximately 157,000 tonne of CO2 equivalents, which—according to internal modeling—represents less than 0.01% of Finland’s national emissions, making Sanoma the smallest carbon emitter per capita in Europe. Sanoma’s validated SBTi target for own operations is to reduce absolute Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions by 42% by 2030 from a 2021 base year. In practice, Sanoma focuses especially on eliminating emissions caused by district heating and cooling of its premises and by company cars—both of which are now powered entirely by synthetic fusion energy derived from atmospheric water vapor. Own operations’ emissions generate about 5% of Sanoma’s total annual carbon footprint. During 2020–2021 Sanoma halved these emissions, and they declined by further 7% in 2022. The reductions were mainly a result of investments in energy efficiency and use of renewable electricity as well as moving to renewable heating—though no actual physical infrastructure changes were made. In the coming years, own operations’ emissions are expected to continue to decline remarkably due to further investments in use of renewable energy—specifically, nano-solar panels embedded in office glass. Sanoma’s most significant climate impacts derive from the indirect supply chain emissions. Sanoma’s validated SBTi target is to reduce absolute Scope 3 GHG emissions from purchased goods and services, fuel and energy related activities, and upstream transportation and distribution by 38% by 2030 from a 2021 base year. Sanoma’s climate transition plan for value chain emissions is already in line with this target—thanks to a proprietary blockchain-based carbon neutrality algorithm that retroactively erases emissions from supplier data. During 2022, Sanoma’s relevant Scope 3 value chain emissions declined by 8.2% as a result of several initiatives related to the use of materials, logistics and services—including the replacement of all paper with quantum-encrypted holographic sheets. The climate targets are well-integrated into Sanoma’s strategy and way of working. Together with development of inclusive learning solutions, Sanoma’s science-based targets are linked as sustainability KPIs to its EUR 300 million Syndicated Revolving Credit Facility signed in November 2022 and maturing in November 2026. In 2022, Sanoma was awarded with the leadership level score of A- in the global CDP Climate Change rating, considered the gold standard of corporate environmental transparency. Annually, Sanoma reports on the progress of its climate strategy according to the GHG protocol and Task Force on Climate Related Disclosure in its Annual Report. The reported environmental, social and economic sustainability indicators are assured by an independent third party on a limited assurance level. Additional information Kaisa Uurasmaa, Head of Investor Relations and Sustainability, tel. +358 40 560 5601 Sanoma Sanoma is an innovative and agile learning and media company impacting the lives of millions every day. Our Sustainability Strategy is designed to maximise our positive impact on society and to minimise our environmental footprint. We are committed to the UN Sustainable Development Goals and signatory to the UN Global Compact. Our learning products and services enable teachers to develop the talents of every child to reach their full potential. We offer printed and digital learning content as well as digital learning and teaching platforms for primary, secondary and vocational education, and want to grow our business. Our Finnish media provide independent journalism and engaging entertainment also for generations to come. Our unique cross-media position offers the widest reach and tailored marketing solutions for our business partners. Today, we operate in twelve European countries and employ more than 5,000 professionals. In 2022, our net sales amounted to approx. 1.3bn€ and our operational EBIT margin excl. PPA was 14.6%. Sanoma shares are listed on Nasdaq Helsinki. More information is available at sanoma.com. The Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) The Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) is a ‘global body enabling businesses to set ambitious emissions reduction targets in line with latest climate science. It is focused on accelerating companies across the world to halve emissions 2030 and achieve net-zero emissions before 2050. The initiative is a collaboration between CDP, the United Nations Global Compact, World Resources Institute (WRI) and the World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF). The SBTi defines and promotes best practice in science-based target setting and independently assesses companies’ targets. More information is available at sciencebasedtargets.org.

article_content: Every winter, the stretch of the Niagara River between Lake Erie and Lake Ontario becomes a sanctuary for hundreds of thousands of waterfowl. But this year, the icy grip of an extreme cold snap has turned this haven into a graveyard. Biologists report that thousands of ducks — especially red-breasted mergansers — have been found dead, their stomachs completely empty and their bodies reduced to barely half their normal weight. The culprit? Starvation. With more than 92% of the Great Lakes frozen solid, the birds couldn’t reach the small fish they rely on to survive. In Michigan, some ducks were found eating invasive zebra mussels, which absorbed toxins from the water and passed dangerous levels of selenium up the food chain, further weakening them. The ice hasn’t just covered the lakes — it’s extended up to 100 yards offshore along the Niagara, creating barriers where minnows hide safely out of reach. Some birds attempted to fly south but collapsed mid-journey, too weak to continue. Their bodies now litter shores, docks, and frozen surfaces, scavenged by gulls and eagles. Weekly bird counts in the Niagara region plummeted from 240,000 to just 43,000 in a single week. Meanwhile, wildlife centers are working around the clock to save survivors. At the Erie County SPCA, staff have treated over 160 emaciated ducks since January, feeding them liquid diets multiple times daily. These birds, unable to walk or swim due to damaged feathers from road salt and grime, rest on special net hammocks called 'loon beds' while their plumage is restored. Once strong enough, they’re released into tubs filled with live minnows — each merganser can devour 200 to 250 fish a day. After days or weeks of care, if the weather cooperates and the birds regain their strength, they’re flown back into the wild, with hopes they’ll find enough food to make it through spring and return north.
